rows.en: Pumas are large, cat-like animals which are found in America.
rows.zh: 美洲狮是一种体型较大、外形像猫的动物，生活在美洲。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When reports came into London Zoo that a wild puma had been spotted forty-five miles south of London, they were not taken seriously.
rows.zh: 伦敦动物园接到报告，说有人在伦敦以南四十五英里的地方发现了一只野生美洲狮，可这些报告起初并未受到重视。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: However, as the evidence began to accumulate, experts from the Zoo felt obliged to investigate, for the descriptions given by people who claimed to have seen the puma were extraordinarily similar.
rows.zh: 然而，随着证据逐渐增多，动物园的专家觉得有必要展开调查，因为那些声称见过美洲狮的人所作的描述极为相似。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The hunt for the puma began in a small village where a woman picking blackberries saw ‘a large cat’ only five yards away from her.
rows.zh: 搜寻美洲狮的行动始于一个小村庄，那里一位正在采摘黑莓的妇女看见一只“大猫”，离她只有五码远。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It immediately ran away when she saw it, and experts confirmed that a puma will not attack a human being unless it is cornered.
rows.zh: 她一看见它，它就立刻跑开了；专家证实，美洲狮除非被逼得走投无路，否则不会攻击人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The search proved difficult, for the puma was often observed at one place in the morning and at another place twenty miles away in the evening.
rows.zh: 搜寻工作十分困难，因为人们常常早晨在一个地方看见它，晚上又在二十英里以外的另一个地方发现它。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Wherever it went, it left behind it a trail of dead deer and small animals like rabbits.
rows.zh: 它无论走到哪里，沿途总会留下死鹿以及兔子等小动物的尸体。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Paw prints were seen in a number of places and puma fur was found clinging to bushes.
rows.zh: 好几个地方都发现了爪印，灌木丛上也找到了挂着的美洲狮毛。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Several people complained of ‘cat-like noises’ at night and a businessman on a fishing trip saw the puma up a tree.
rows.zh: 有几个人抱怨夜里听见“像猫叫一样的声音”，还有一位出门钓鱼的商人看见那只美洲狮在树上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The experts were now fully convinced that the animal was a puma, but where had it come from?
rows.zh: 专家这时完全确信那动物是一只美洲狮，可它究竟是从哪里来的呢？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As no pumas had been reported missing from any zoo in the country, this one must have been in the possession of a private collector and somehow managed to escape.
rows.zh: 国内没有一家动物园报告有美洲狮失踪，所以这只美洲狮一定曾由私人收藏者饲养，不知怎样设法逃了出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The hunt went on for several weeks, but the puma was not caught.
rows.zh: 搜寻持续了好几个星期，却始终没有抓到那只美洲狮。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is disturbing to think that a dangerous wild animal is still at large in the quiet countryside.
rows.zh: 想到一只危险的野兽还在宁静的乡间四处游荡，实在令人不安。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 常用 take somebody/something seriously；被动形式为 be taken seriously。
usage.example: When reports came into London Zoo that a wild puma had been spotted forty-five miles south of London, they were not taken seriously.
usage.exampleZh: 伦敦动物园接到报告，说有人在伦敦以南四十五英里的地方发现了一只野生美洲狮，可这些报告起初并未受到重视。

usage.meaning: 觉得有责任或有必要做某事
usage.note: obliged 表示受到责任或情势的推动，后接 to 加动词原形。
usage.example: However, as the evidence began to accumulate, experts from the Zoo felt obliged to investigate, for the descriptions given by people who claimed to have seen the puma were extraordinarily similar.
usage.exampleZh: 然而，随着证据逐渐增多，动物园的专家觉得有必要展开调查，因为那些声称见过美洲狮的人所作的描述极为相似。

usage.note: 可指离去后留下的痕迹、物品或后果；本文代词 it 指美洲狮。
usage.example: Wherever it went, it left behind it a trail of dead deer and small animals like rabbits.
usage.exampleZh: 它无论走到哪里，沿途总会留下死鹿以及兔子等小动物的尸体。

usage.note: in the possession of somebody 表示东西归某人所有；in possession of 则以拥有者为主语。
usage.example: As no pumas had been reported missing from any zoo in the country, this one must have been in the possession of a private collector and somehow managed to escape.
usage.exampleZh: 国内没有一家动物园报告有美洲狮失踪，所以这只美洲狮一定曾由私人收藏者饲养，不知怎样设法逃了出来。

usage.note: 用于逃犯或危险动物时，表示尚未受到拘捕或控制。
usage.example: It is disturbing to think that a dangerous wild animal is still at large in the quiet countryside.
usage.exampleZh: 想到一只危险的野兽还在宁静的乡间四处游荡，实在令人不安。

rows.en: Our vicar is always raising money for one cause or another, but he has never managed to get enough money to have the church clock repaired.
rows.zh: 我们教区的牧师总在为这样那样的事情筹款，可他始终没能筹到足够的钱来修理教堂的大钟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The big clock which used to strike the hours day and night was damaged many years ago and has been silent ever since.
rows.zh: 那座大钟从前昼夜报时，多年前损坏之后，就一直没有再响过。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One night, however, our vicar woke up with a start: the clock was striking the hours!
rows.zh: 然而，一天夜里，我们的牧师突然惊醒了：大钟竟然在报时！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Looking at his watch, he saw that it was one o’clock, but the bell struck thirteen times before it stopped.
rows.zh: 他看了看表，发现当时是一点，可钟声响了十三下才停。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Armed with a torch, the vicar went up into the clock tower to see what was going on.
rows.zh: 牧师拿着手电筒，走上钟楼，想看看究竟出了什么事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the torchlight, he caught sight of a figure whom he immediately recognized as Bill Wilkins, our local grocer.
rows.zh: 手电筒的光照出一个人影，他立刻认出那是本地的杂货店老板比尔·威尔金斯。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: ‘Whatever are you doing up here Bill?’ asked the vicar in surprise.
rows.zh: “比尔，你到底在这上头干什么？”牧师惊讶地问。
rows.speaker: 牧师

rows.en: ‘I’m trying to repair the bell,’ answered Bill.
rows.zh: “我在试着修钟，”比尔答道。
rows.speaker: 比尔·威尔金斯

rows.en: ‘I've been coming up here night after night for weeks now.
rows.zh: “这几个星期，我每天晚上都上这儿来。
rows.speaker: 比尔·威尔金斯

rows.en: You see, I was hoping to give you a surprise.’
rows.zh: 你知道，我原本想给您一个惊喜。”
rows.speaker: 比尔·威尔金斯

rows.en: ‘You certainly did give me a surprise!’ said the vicar.
rows.zh: “你可真让我大吃了一惊！”牧师说。
rows.speaker: 牧师

rows.en: ‘You've probably woken up everyone in the village as well.
rows.zh: “你大概也把全村人都吵醒了。
rows.speaker: 牧师

rows.en: Still, I'm glad the bell is working again.’
rows.zh: 不过，钟又能响了，我还是很高兴。”
rows.speaker: 牧师

rows.en: ‘That's the trouble, vicar,’ answered Bill.
rows.zh: “麻烦就在这儿，牧师，”比尔回答。
rows.speaker: 比尔·威尔金斯

rows.en: ‘It’s working all right, but I'm afraid that at one o’clock it will strike thirteen times and there’s nothing I can do about it.’
rows.zh: “钟倒是能响了，可恐怕到了一点它就要敲十三下，这一点我实在无能为力。”
rows.speaker: 比尔·威尔金斯

rows.en: ‘We'll get used to that, Bill,’ said the vicar.
rows.zh: “我们会习惯的，比尔，”牧师说。
rows.speaker: 牧师

rows.en: ‘Thirteen is not as good as one, but it's better than nothing.
rows.zh: “十三下虽然不如一下好，可总比一下都不响强。
rows.speaker: 牧师

rows.en: Now let’s go downstairs and have a cup of tea.’
rows.zh: 现在咱们下楼喝杯茶吧。”
rows.speaker: 牧师

usage.note: one 后的名词可替换，表示种类不一且未具体指明的事物。
usage.example: Our vicar is always raising money for one cause or another, but he has never managed to get enough money to have the church clock repaired.
usage.exampleZh: 我们教区的牧师总在为这样那样的事情筹款，可他始终没能筹到足够的钱来修理教堂的大钟。

usage.note: 可直接作时间状语，强调白天和夜间都如此。
usage.example: The big clock which used to strike the hours day and night was damaged many years ago and has been silent ever since.
usage.exampleZh: 那座大钟从前昼夜报时，多年前损坏之后，就一直没有再响过。

usage.note: 常与 wake up 搭配，表示突然受惊而醒。
usage.example: One night, however, our vicar woke up with a start: the clock was striking the hours!
usage.exampleZh: 然而，一天夜里，我们的牧师突然惊醒了：大钟竟然在报时！

usage.note: 强调某人或某物进入视野；不要与表示持续观察的 watch 混淆。
usage.example: In the torchlight, he caught sight of a figure whom he immediately recognized as Bill Wilkins, our local grocer.
usage.exampleZh: 手电筒的光照出一个人影，他立刻认出那是本地的杂货店老板比尔·威尔金斯。

usage.note: 名词重复搭配 after，突出反复持续，如 day after day。
usage.example: ‘I've been coming up here night after night for weeks now.
usage.exampleZh: “这几个星期，我每天晚上都上这儿来。

usage.note: to 是介词，后接名词、代词或动名词，不能直接接动词原形。
usage.example: ‘We'll get used to that, Bill,’ said the vicar.
usage.exampleZh: “我们会习惯的，比尔，”牧师说。

rows.en: Some time ago, an interesting discovery was made by archaeologists on the Aegean island of Kea.
rows.zh: 前些时候，考古学家在爱琴海的凯阿岛上有了一项有趣的发现。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: An American team explored a temple which stands in an ancient city on the promontory of Ayia Irini.
rows.zh: 一支美国考古队考察了一座神庙，它位于阿伊亚伊里尼海角的一座古城里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The city at one time must have been prosperous, for it enjoyed a high level of civilization.
rows.zh: 这座城市一度一定十分繁荣，因为它曾拥有高度发达的文明。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Houses — often three storeys high — were built of stone.
rows.zh: 房屋用石头建成，往往高达三层。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They had large rooms with beautifully decorated walls.
rows.zh: 屋内的房间宽敞，墙壁装饰精美。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The city was even equipped with a drainage system, for a great many clay pipes were found beneath the narrow streets.
rows.zh: 这座城市甚至配备了排水系统，因为在狭窄的街道下面发现了大量陶制管道。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The temple which the archaeologists explored was used as a place of worship from the fifteenth century B.C. until Roman times.
rows.zh: 考古学家考察的这座神庙，从公元前十五世纪一直到古罗马时期都被用作礼拜场所。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the most sacred room of the temple, clay fragments of fifteen statues were found.
rows.zh: 在神庙最神圣的房间里，发现了十五尊雕像的陶制碎片。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Each of these represented a goddess and had, at one time, been painted.
rows.zh: 每尊雕像表现的都是一位女神，而且都曾经上过色。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The body of one statue was found among remains dating from the fifteenth century B.C.
rows.zh: 其中一尊雕像的躯干是在公元前十五世纪的遗存中发现的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Its missing head happened to be among remains of the fifth century B.C.
rows.zh: 它缺失的头部恰好出现在公元前五世纪的遗存中。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This head must have been found in Classical times and carefully preserved.
rows.zh: 这颗头像一定是在古典时代被发现，随后得到了精心保存。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was very old and precious even then.
rows.zh: 即使在当时，它也已经十分古老而珍贵了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When the archaeologists reconstructed the fragments, they were amazed to find that the goddess turned out to be a very modern-looking woman.
rows.zh: 考古学家把碎片重新拼合起来后，惊讶地发现，这位女神竟是一位相貌十分现代的女子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She stood three feet high and her hands rested on her hips.
rows.zh: 她高三英尺，双手叉在腰间。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She was wearing a full-length skirt which swept the ground.
rows.zh: 她穿着一条曳地的长裙。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Despite her great age, she was very graceful indeed, but, so far, the archaeologists have been unable to discover her identity.
rows.zh: 虽然年代久远，她的姿态确实依旧十分优雅；不过，考古学家至今还未能查明她的身份。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 这里指过去某一时期，不是“同时”；表示同时通常用 at the same time。
usage.example: The city at one time must have been prosperous, for it enjoyed a high level of civilization.
usage.exampleZh: 这座城市一度一定十分繁荣，因为它曾拥有高度发达的文明。

usage.note: equipment 为不可数名词；be equipped with 后接配备的设施或设备。
usage.example: The city was even equipped with a drainage system, for a great many clay pipes were found beneath the narrow streets.
usage.exampleZh: 这座城市甚至配备了排水系统，因为在狭窄的街道下面发现了大量陶制管道。

usage.note: date from 后接起始时间，本文分词短语修饰 remains。
usage.example: The body of one statue was found among remains dating from the fifteenth century B.C.
usage.exampleZh: 其中一尊雕像的躯干是在公元前十五世纪的遗存中发现的。

usage.note: 常用于最终结果出乎预料的情形，后接名词或形容词。
usage.example: When the archaeologists reconstructed the fragments, they were amazed to find that the goddess turned out to be a very modern-looking woman.
usage.exampleZh: 考古学家把碎片重新拼合起来后，惊讶地发现，这位女神竟是一位相貌十分现代的女子。

usage.note: 强调从过去延续到现在的情况，常与现在完成时连用。
usage.example: Despite her great age, she was very graceful indeed, but, so far, the archaeologists have been unable to discover her identity.
usage.exampleZh: 虽然年代久远，她的姿态确实依旧十分优雅；不过，考古学家至今还未能查明她的身份。

lessons.title: The double life of Alfred Bloggs

rows.en: These days, people who do manual work often receive far more money than people who work in offices.
rows.zh: 如今，从事体力劳动的人，收入往往比坐办公室的人高得多。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: People who work in offices are frequently referred to as ‘white-collar workers’ for the simple reason that they usually wear a collar and tie to go to work.
rows.zh: 办公室工作人员常被称为“白领”，原因很简单：他们上班通常穿有领衬衫、打领带。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Such is human nature, that a great many people are often willing to sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming white-collar workers.
rows.zh: 人性就是如此，许多人往往情愿放弃较高的薪水，以换取成为白领的那份体面。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This can give rise to curious situations, as it did in the case of Alfred Bloggs who worked as a dustman for the Ellesmere Corporation.
rows.zh: 这会造成一些奇特的情况，埃尔斯米尔市政机构的清洁工阿尔弗雷德·布洛格斯就是一例。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When he got married, Alf was too embarrassed to say anything to his wife about his job.
rows.zh: 阿尔弗结婚时，不好意思向妻子提起自己的工作。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He simply told her that he worked for the Corporation.
rows.zh: 他只告诉她，自己在市政机构工作。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Every morning, he left home dressed in a smart black suit.
rows.zh: 每天早上，他都穿着一套挺括的黑西装离家。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He then changed into overalls and spent the next eight hours as a dustman.
rows.zh: 然后，他换上工作服，接下来的八小时就当清洁工。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Before returning home at night, he took a shower and changed back into his suit.
rows.zh: 晚上回家前，他先洗个澡，再换回西装。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Alf did this for over two years and his fellow dustmen kept his secret.
rows.zh: 阿尔弗这样做了两年多，清洁工同事们也一直替他保守秘密。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Alf’s wife has never discovered that she married a dustman and she never will, for Alf has just found another job.
rows.zh: 阿尔弗的妻子始终没有发现自己嫁给了一名清洁工，而且以后也永远不会发现，因为阿尔弗刚找到了一份新工作。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He will soon be working in an office.
rows.zh: 他很快就要到办公室工作了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He will be earning only half as much as he used to, but he feels that his rise in status is well worth the loss of money.
rows.zh: 他的收入将只有过去的一半，但他觉得，地位的提高完全值得这笔金钱上的损失。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From now on, he will wear a suit all day and others will call him ‘Mr. Bloggs’, not ‘Alf’.
rows.zh: 从今以后，他将整天穿着西装，别人也会称呼他“布洛格斯先生”，而不再叫他“阿尔弗”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: manual 在此指依靠体力或双手完成的工作；work 为不可数名词。
usage.example: These days, people who do manual work often receive far more money than people who work in offices.
usage.exampleZh: 如今，从事体力劳动的人，收入往往比坐办公室的人高得多。

usage.note: 常见被动结构 be referred to as；as 后接名称或称谓。
usage.example: People who work in offices are frequently referred to as ‘white-collar workers’ for the simple reason that they usually wear a collar and tie to go to work.
usage.exampleZh: 办公室工作人员常被称为“白领”，原因很简单：他们上班通常穿有领衬衫、打领带。

usage.note: 后接结果、问题或情况，语气较正式。
usage.example: This can give rise to curious situations, as it did in the case of Alfred Bloggs who worked as a dustman for the Ellesmere Corporation.
usage.exampleZh: 这会造成一些奇特的情况，埃尔斯米尔市政机构的清洁工阿尔弗雷德·布洛格斯就是一例。

usage.note: 表示换穿某种衣物；change back into 表示换回原来的衣服。
usage.example: He then changed into overalls and spent the next eight hours as a dustman.
usage.exampleZh: 然后，他换上工作服，接下来的八小时就当清洁工。

usage.note: worth 后接名词或动名词，well 可加强语气，不用 very 修饰 worth。
usage.example: He will be earning only half as much as he used to, but he feels that his rise in status is well worth the loss of money.
usage.exampleZh: 他的收入将只有过去的一半，但他觉得，地位的提高完全值得这笔金钱上的损失。

usage.note: 强调某一做法或状态从说话所指的现在开始持续。
usage.example: From now on, he will wear a suit all day and others will call him ‘Mr. Bloggs’, not ‘Alf’.
usage.exampleZh: 从今以后，他将整天穿着西装，别人也会称呼他“布洛格斯先生”，而不再叫他“阿尔弗”。

rows.en: Editors of newspapers and magazines often go to extremes to provide their readers with unimportant facts and statistics.
rows.zh: 报刊编辑为了向读者提供一些无关紧要的事实和统计数字，常常不惜走极端。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Last year a journalist had been instructed by a well-known magazine to write an article on the president’s palace in a new African republic.
rows.zh: 去年，一家知名杂志要求一名记者写一篇文章，介绍非洲一个新成立的共和国的总统府。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When the article arrived, the editor read the first sentence and then refused to publish it.
rows.zh: 稿子送到后，编辑读了第一句话，就拒绝刊登。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The article began: ‘Hundreds of steps lead to the high wall which surrounds the president's palace.’
rows.zh: 文章开头写道：“数百级台阶通向环绕总统府的高墙。”
rows.speaker: 记者（文章原文）

rows.en: The editor at once sent the journalist a fax instructing him to find out the exact number of steps and the height of the wall.
rows.zh: 编辑立即给记者发了一份传真，要求他查清台阶的准确级数以及围墙的高度。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The journalist immediately set out to obtain these important facts, but he took a long time to send them.
rows.zh: 记者立刻着手获取这些重要事实，可是过了很久也没把它们发回来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Meanwhile, the editor was getting impatient, for the magazine would soon go to press.
rows.zh: 与此同时，编辑越来越不耐烦，因为杂志很快就要付印了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He sent the journalist two more faxes, but received no reply.
rows.zh: 他又给记者发了两份传真，却没有收到答复。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He sent yet another fax informing the journalist that if he did not reply soon he would be fired.
rows.zh: 他再发了一份传真，告诉记者，要是不尽快答复，就会被解雇。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When the journalist again failed to reply, the editor reluctantly published the article as it had originally been written.
rows.zh: 记者仍然没有回复，编辑只好不情愿地照原稿刊登了文章。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A week later, the editor at last received a fax from the journalist.
rows.zh: 一周后，编辑终于收到了记者的传真。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Not only had the poor man been arrested, but he had been sent to prison as well.
rows.zh: 原来，这个可怜的人不仅被逮捕了，还被关进了监狱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: However, he had at last been allowed to send a fax in which he informed the editor that he had been arrested while counting the 1,084 steps leading to the fifteen-foot wall which surrounded the president’s palace.
rows.zh: 不过，他终于获准发一份传真，在传真中告诉编辑：他是在数通往总统府十五英尺高围墙的那一千零八十四级台阶时被逮捕的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.meaning: 走极端，采取过火的做法
usage.note: 常接 to do something，说明为了什么而做得过头。
usage.example: Editors of newspapers and magazines often go to extremes to provide their readers with unimportant facts and statistics.
usage.exampleZh: 报刊编辑为了向读者提供一些无关紧要的事实和统计数字，常常不惜走极端。

usage.note: 强调通过调查或询问获知事实，后可接名词或疑问词引导的从句。
usage.example: The editor at once sent the journalist a fax instructing him to find out the exact number of steps and the height of the wall.
usage.exampleZh: 编辑立即给记者发了一份传真，要求他查清台阶的准确级数以及围墙的高度。

usage.note: set out to 加动词原形表示开始执行一项有目的的行动。
usage.example: The journalist immediately set out to obtain these important facts, but he took a long time to send them.
usage.exampleZh: 记者立刻着手获取这些重要事实，可是过了很久也没把它们发回来。

usage.note: 用于报刊书籍进入印刷阶段；press 在这一固定搭配中不加冠词。
usage.example: Meanwhile, the editor was getting impatient, for the magazine would soon go to press.
usage.exampleZh: 与此同时，编辑越来越不耐烦，因为杂志很快就要付印了。

usage.note: 通常放在句末；本句与 not only ... but ... 连用，补充被送进监狱这一遭遇。
usage.example: Not only had the poor man been arrested, but he had been sent to prison as well.
usage.exampleZh: 原来，这个可怜的人不仅被逮捕了，还被关进了监狱。

usage.note: 强调等候或拖延之后某件事终于发生，常带如释重负或不耐的语气。
usage.example: A week later, the editor at last received a fax from the journalist.
usage.exampleZh: 一周后，编辑终于收到了记者的传真。

rows.en: The expensive shops in a famous arcade near Piccadilly were just opening.
rows.zh: 皮卡迪利附近一条著名购物廊里的高档商店刚刚开门营业。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At this time of the morning, the arcade was almost empty.
rows.zh: 早晨这个时候，购物廊里几乎没有人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mr. Taylor, the owner of a jewellery shop was admiring a new window display.
rows.zh: 一家珠宝店的店主泰勒先生，正在欣赏新布置的橱窗。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Two of his assistants had been working busily since eight o’clock and had only just finished.
rows.zh: 他的两名店员从八点起就一直忙着布置，刚刚才完工。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Diamond necklaces and rings had been beautifully arranged on a background of black velvet.
rows.zh: 钻石项链和戒指以黑色天鹅绒为衬底，摆放得十分漂亮。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After gazing at the display for several minutes, Mr. Taylor went back into his shop.
rows.zh: 泰勒先生凝视了这番陈列几分钟后，回到了店里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The silence was suddenly broken when a large car, with its headlights on and its horn blaring, roared down the arcade.
rows.zh: 突然，一辆大汽车亮着前灯、鸣着喇叭，沿购物廊呼啸驶来，打破了寂静。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It came to a stop outside the jeweller’s.
rows.zh: 车停在了珠宝店外。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One man stayed at the wheel while two others with black stockings over their faces jumped out and smashed the window of the shop with iron bars.
rows.zh: 一个人留在驾驶座上，另外两个人脸上套着黑色长袜，跳下车来，用铁棒砸碎了商店的橱窗。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: While this was going on, Mr. Taylor was upstairs.
rows.zh: 这一切发生的时候，泰勒先生正在楼上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He and his staff began throwing furniture out of the window.
rows.zh: 他和店员开始把家具从窗口往外扔。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Chairs and tables went flying into the arcade.
rows.zh: 椅子和桌子纷纷飞进购物廊。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One of the thieves was struck by a heavy statue, but he was too busy helping himself to diamonds to notice any pain.
rows.zh: 一尊沉重的雕像砸中了一个窃贼，可他正忙着大把拿钻石，根本顾不上疼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The raid was all over in three minutes, for the men scrambled back into the car and it moved off at a fantastic speed.
rows.zh: 整个抢劫过程三分钟就结束了，那几个人仓促爬回车里，车以惊人的速度开走了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Just as it was leaving, Mr. Taylor rushed out and ran after it throwing ashtrays and vases, but it was impossible to stop the thieves.
rows.zh: 就在车开走时，泰勒先生冲了出来，追着汽车扔烟灰缸和花瓶，可已经无法拦住那些窃贼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They had got away with thousands of pounds worth of diamonds.
rows.zh: 他们带着价值数千英镑的钻石逃掉了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 表示目光停留较久；at 后接注视的对象。
usage.example: After gazing at the display for several minutes, Mr. Taylor went back into his shop.
usage.exampleZh: 泰勒先生凝视了这番陈列几分钟后，回到了店里。

usage.note: 描述从移动到停止的过程，stop 在这里是名词。
usage.example: It came to a stop outside the jeweller’s.
usage.exampleZh: 车停在了珠宝店外。

usage.note: wheel 在这一搭配中指汽车方向盘，常暗示某人正负责驾驶。
usage.example: One man stayed at the wheel while two others with black stockings over their faces jumped out and smashed the window of the shop with iron bars.
usage.exampleZh: 一个人留在驾驶座上，另外两个人脸上套着黑色长袜，跳下车来，用铁棒砸碎了商店的橱窗。

usage.meaning: 自行取用；此处指大肆拿走
usage.note: 通常用于招呼人自行取食，文中带讽刺意味，指窃贼擅自拿取珠宝。
usage.example: One of the thieves was struck by a heavy statue, but he was too busy helping himself to diamonds to notice any pain.
usage.exampleZh: 一尊沉重的雕像砸中了一个窃贼，可他正忙着大把拿钻石，根本顾不上疼。

usage.note: 这里 with 后接偷走的物品；也可用于表示做坏事而未受惩罚，需按语境区分。
usage.example: They had got away with thousands of pounds worth of diamonds.
usage.exampleZh: 他们带着价值数千英镑的钻石逃掉了。

lessons.title: Mutilated ladies

rows.en: Has it ever happened to you?
rows.zh: 你碰到过这种事吗？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Have you ever put your trousers in the washing machine and then remembered there was a large bank note in your back pocket?
rows.zh: 你有没有把裤子放进洗衣机后，才想起后裤袋里还有一张大面额钞票？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When you rescued your trousers, did you find the note was whiter than white?
rows.zh: 等你把裤子抢救出来时，有没有发现钞票已经洗得白得不能再白了？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: People who live in Britain needn’t despair when they make mistakes like this (and a lot of people do)!
rows.zh: 住在英国的人犯下这种错误时不必绝望，而犯这种错误的人还真不少！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Fortunately for them, the Bank of England has a team called Mutilated Ladies which deals with claims from people who fed their money to a machine or to their dog.
rows.zh: 对他们来说，幸运的是，英格兰银行有一个名叫“残损纸币处理小组”（Mutilated Ladies）的团队，负责处理那些把钞票送进机器或狗嘴的人提出的兑换申请。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Dogs, it seems, love to chew up money!
rows.zh: 狗似乎特别喜欢把钞票嚼得粉碎！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A recent case concerns Jane Butlin whose fiancé, John, runs a successful furniture business.
rows.zh: 最近的一桩案例与简·巴特林有关，她的未婚夫约翰经营着一家生意兴隆的家具公司。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: John had a very good day and put his wallet containing £ 3,000 into the microwave oven for safekeeping.
rows.zh: 约翰那天生意特别好，为了安全起见，他把装着三千英镑的钱包放进了微波炉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Then he and Jane went horse-riding.
rows.zh: 随后，他和简骑马去了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When they got home, Jane cooked their dinner in the microwave oven and without realizing it, cooked her fiancé’s wallet as well.
rows.zh: 回家后，简用微波炉做晚饭，无意之中也把未婚夫的钱包一块儿烤了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Imagine their dismay when they found a beautifully-cooked wallet and notes turned to ash!
rows.zh: 想象一下，他们发现钱包“烤得恰到好处”、钞票却化成灰烬时，会多么沮丧！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: John went to see his bank manager who sent the remains of wallet and the money to the special department of the Bank of England in Newcastle: the Mutilated Ladies!
rows.zh: 约翰去找银行经理，经理把钱包和钞票的残骸送到了英格兰银行设在纽卡斯尔的那个特别部门——残损纸币处理小组！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They examined the remains and John got all his money back.
rows.zh: 他们检查了这些残骸，约翰便拿回了全部款项。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: ‘So long as there’s something to identify, we will give people their money back,’ said a spokeswoman for the Bank.
rows.zh: 银行的一位女发言人说：“只要还剩下可以辨认的东西，我们就会把钱退还给人们。”
rows.speaker: 英格兰银行女发言人

rows.en: ‘Last year, we paid £1.5m on 21,000 claims.’
rows.zh: “去年，我们受理了两万一千宗申请，兑付了一百五十万英镑。”
rows.speaker: 英格兰银行女发言人

usage.note: deal with 后接需要处理的人或事；本文 claims 指残损钞票的兑付申请。
usage.example: Fortunately for them, the Bank of England has a team called Mutilated Ladies which deals with claims from people who fed their money to a machine or to their dog.
usage.exampleZh: 对他们来说，幸运的是，英格兰银行有一个名叫“残损纸币处理小组”（Mutilated Ladies）的团队，负责处理那些把钞票送进机器或狗嘴的人提出的兑换申请。

usage.note: up 强调嚼得破碎或彻底，money 在此具体指纸币。
usage.example: Dogs, it seems, love to chew up money!
usage.exampleZh: 狗似乎特别喜欢把钞票嚼得粉碎！

usage.note: 常用于将钱或贵重物品放置、交托到某处，表示保管目的。
usage.example: John had a very good day and put his wallet containing £ 3,000 into the microwave oven for safekeeping.
usage.exampleZh: 约翰那天生意特别好，为了安全起见，他把装着三千英镑的钱包放进了微波炉。

usage.note: without 为介词，后接动名词；it 指当事人未察觉的情况。
usage.example: When they got home, Jane cooked their dinner in the microwave oven and without realizing it, cooked her fiancé’s wallet as well.
usage.exampleZh: 回家后，简用微波炉做晚饭，无意之中也把未婚夫的钱包一块儿烤了。

usage.note: 引导条件从句，与 as long as 在这一用法中相近，不是比较持续时间。
usage.example: ‘So long as there’s something to identify, we will give people their money back,’ said a spokeswoman for the Bank.
usage.exampleZh: 银行的一位女发言人说：“只要还剩下可以辨认的东西，我们就会把钱退还给人们。”

translationNotes: Mutilated Ladies 是原文对银行残损钞票处理团队的诙谐称呼；译文按其职能译为“残损纸币处理小组”，同时保留英文名称。

rows.en: The Great St. Bernard Pass connects Switzerland to Italy.
rows.zh: 大圣伯纳德山口连接着瑞士和意大利。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At 2,473 metres, it is the highest mountain pass in Europe.
rows.zh: 它海拔两千四百七十三米，是欧洲最高的山口。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The famous monastery of St. Bernard, which was founded in the eleventh century, lies about a mile away.
rows.zh: 著名的圣伯纳德修道院创建于十一世纪，位于大约一英里之外。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For hundreds of years, St. Bernard dogs have saved the lives of travellers crossing the dangerous Pass.
rows.zh: 几百年来，圣伯纳德犬救过许多穿越这处险峻山口的旅行者的性命。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These friendly dogs, which were first brought from Asia, were used as watchdogs even in Roman times.
rows.zh: 这些友善的狗最初从亚洲引进，早在古罗马时期就被用来看家护院。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Now that a tunnel has been built through the mountains, the Pass is less dangerous, but each year, the dogs are still sent out into the snow whenever a traveller is in difficulty.
rows.zh: 如今，穿山隧道已经建成，山口的危险性有所降低，但每年只要有旅行者遇险，这些狗仍会被派到雪地里救援。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Despite the new tunnel, there are still a few people who rashly attempt to cross the Pass on foot.
rows.zh: 尽管有了新隧道，仍有少数人冒失地试图徒步穿越山口。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: During the summer months, the monastery is very busy, for it is visited by thousands of people who cross the Pass in cars.
rows.zh: 夏季的几个月里，修道院非常热闹，因为有成千上万开车经过山口的人来参观。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As there are so many people about, the dogs have to be kept in a special enclosure.
rows.zh: 由于周围人太多，这些狗只得关在专门的围栏内。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In winter, however, life at the monastery is quite different.
rows.zh: 然而到了冬天，修道院里的生活就大不一样了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The temperature drops to -30° and very few people attempt to cross the Pass.
rows.zh: 气温降到零下三十度，极少有人尝试穿越山口。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The monks prefer winter to summer for they have more privacy.
rows.zh: 修士们更喜欢冬天，而不喜欢夏天，因为冬天他们能有更多不受打扰的私人空间。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The dogs have greater freedom, too, for they are allowed to wander outside their enclosure.
rows.zh: 狗也有了更大的自由，因为它们获准在围栏外四处走动。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The only regular visitors to the monastery in winter are parties of skiers who go there at Christmas and Easter.
rows.zh: 冬天定期造访修道院的，只有在圣诞节和复活节前来的一群群滑雪者。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These young people, who love the peace of the mountains, always receive a warm welcome at St. Bernard's monastery.
rows.zh: 这些热爱山中宁静的年轻人，在圣伯纳德修道院总会受到热情欢迎。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: connect A to B 表示把 A 与 B 相连；此处主语是连接两地的山口。
usage.example: The Great St. Bernard Pass connects Switzerland to Italy.
usage.exampleZh: 大圣伯纳德山口连接着瑞士和意大利。

usage.note: 引导原因从句，强调新的情况已经出现，从而带来后面的结果。
usage.example: Now that a tunnel has been built through the mountains, the Pass is less dangerous, but each year, the dogs are still sent out into the snow whenever a traveller is in difficulty.
usage.exampleZh: 如今，穿山隧道已经建成，山口的危险性有所降低，但每年只要有旅行者遇险，这些狗仍会被派到雪地里救援。

usage.note: 本文指旅行者遇险；也可用于一般生活或工作上的困难。
usage.example: Now that a tunnel has been built through the mountains, the Pass is less dangerous, but each year, the dogs are still sent out into the snow whenever a traveller is in difficulty.
usage.exampleZh: 如今，穿山隧道已经建成，山口的危险性有所降低，但每年只要有旅行者遇险，这些狗仍会被派到雪地里救援。

usage.note: 固定搭配不加冠词，也不用复数 feet。
usage.example: Despite the new tunnel, there are still a few people who rashly attempt to cross the Pass on foot.
usage.exampleZh: 尽管有了新隧道，仍有少数人冒失地试图徒步穿越山口。

usage.note: prefer A to B 中 A 是更喜欢的对象，to 是介词。
usage.example: The monks prefer winter to summer for they have more privacy.
usage.exampleZh: 修士们更喜欢冬天，而不喜欢夏天，因为冬天他们能有更多不受打扰的私人空间。

usage.note: welcome 在此为可数名词；give somebody a warm welcome 表示热情欢迎某人。
usage.example: These young people, who love the peace of the mountains, always receive a warm welcome at St. Bernard's monastery.
usage.exampleZh: 这些热爱山中宁静的年轻人，在圣伯纳德修道院总会受到热情欢迎。

rows.en: Cats never fail to fascinate human beings.
rows.zh: 猫总能让人着迷。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They can be friendly and affectionate towards humans, but they lead mysterious lives of their own as well.
rows.zh: 它们可以对人友善而亲昵，但也过着自己神秘的生活。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They never become submissive like dogs and horses.
rows.zh: 它们从不像狗和马那样变得顺从。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As a result, humans have learned to respect feline independence.
rows.zh: 因此，人类已学会尊重猫的独立性。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Most cats remain suspicious of humans all their lives.
rows.zh: 大多数猫终其一生都对人类保持戒心。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One of the things that fascinates us most about cats is the popular belief that they have nine lives.
rows.zh: 猫最让我们着迷的地方之一，就是人们普遍相信它们有九条命。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Apparently, there is a good deal of truth in this idea.
rows.zh: 看来，这种说法还真有不少道理。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A cat’s ability to survive falls is based on fact.
rows.zh: 猫能够从高处坠落后生还，是有事实依据的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Recently the New York Animal Medical Centre made a study of 132 cats over a period of five months.
rows.zh: 最近，纽约动物医疗中心在五个月里对一百三十二只猫进行了研究。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All these cats had one experience in common: they had fallen off high buildings, yet only eight of them died from shock or injuries.
rows.zh: 这些猫都有一个共同经历：从高楼坠落过，然而其中只有八只因休克或伤势而死亡。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Of course, New York is the ideal place for such an interesting study, because there is no shortage of tall buildings.
rows.zh: 当然，纽约是开展这种有趣研究的理想地点，因为那里不缺高楼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There are plenty of high-rise windowsills to fall from!
rows.zh: 有的是可供猫跌落的高层窗台！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One cat, Sabrina, fell 32 storeys, yet only suffered from a broken tooth.
rows.zh: 一只名叫萨布丽娜的猫从三十二层楼的高度跌落，却只摔断了一颗牙。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: ‘Cats behave like well-trained paratroopers,’ a doctor said.
rows.zh: 一位医生说：“猫的表现就像训练有素的伞兵。”
rows.speaker: 一位医生

rows.en: It seems that the further cats fall, the less they are likely to injure themselves.
rows.zh: 看起来，猫下落的距离越长，受伤的可能性反而越小。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In a long drop, they reach speeds of 60 miles an hour and more.
rows.zh: 长距离坠落时，它们的速度会达到每小时六十英里，甚至更快。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At high speeds, falling cats have time to relax.
rows.zh: 下落速度很高时，猫有时间放松身体。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They stretch out their legs like flying squirrels.
rows.zh: 它们像鼯鼠一样伸展开四肢。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This increases their air-resistance and reduces the shock of impact when they hit the ground.
rows.zh: 这样会增加空气阻力，减轻落地瞬间的冲击。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 字面为从不未能做到，实际强调每次都能产生某种效果，注意双重否定。
usage.example: Cats never fail to fascinate human beings.
usage.exampleZh: 猫总能让人着迷。

usage.note: 作连接性状语时可单独使用；as a result of 后要接原因。
usage.example: As a result, humans have learned to respect feline independence.
usage.exampleZh: 因此，人类已学会尊重猫的独立性。

usage.note: suspicious of 表示不信任或有疑心，不等于令人怀疑的 suspicious 人或行为。
usage.example: Most cats remain suspicious of humans all their lives.
usage.exampleZh: 大多数猫终其一生都对人类保持戒心。

usage.exampleZh: 当然，纽约是开展这种有趣研究的理想地点，因为那里不缺高楼。

usage.exampleZh: 它们像鼯鼠一样伸展开四肢。

rows.en: The great ship, Titanic, sailed for New York from Southampton on April 10th, 1912.
rows.zh: 巨轮“泰坦尼克号”于一九一二年四月十日从南安普敦起航，驶往纽约。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She was carrying 1,316 passengers and a crew of 891.
rows.zh: 船上载有一千三百一十六名乘客和八百九十一名船员。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even by modern standards, the 46,000 ton Titanic was a colossal ship.
rows.zh: 即使按现代标准衡量，这艘四万六千吨的“泰坦尼克号”也称得上巨轮。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At that time, however, she was not only the largest ship that had ever been built, but was regarded as unsinkable, for she had sixteen watertight compartments.
rows.zh: 而在当时，它不仅是有史以来建造的最大船只，还被认为永不沉没，因为船上设有十六个水密舱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even if two of these were flooded, she would still be able to float.
rows.zh: 即使其中两个进水，船仍然能够漂浮。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The tragic sinking of this great liner will always be remembered, for she went down on her first voyage with heavy loss of life.
rows.zh: 这艘巨型客轮悲惨沉没的事件将永远被人铭记，因为它在首次航行中就沉入海底，造成大量人员丧生。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Four days after setting out, while the Titanic was sailing across the icy waters of the North Atlantic, a huge iceberg was suddenly spotted by a lookout.
rows.zh: 起航四天后，“泰坦尼克号”正在北大西洋冰冷的海域航行，一名瞭望员突然发现了一座巨大的冰山。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After the alarm had been given, the great ship turned sharply to avoid a direct collision.
rows.zh: 警报发出后，巨轮猛地转向，以避免正面相撞。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Titanic turned just in time, narrowly missing the immense wall of ice which rose over 100 feet out of the water beside her.
rows.zh: “泰坦尼克号”及时转了向，险些撞上身旁那堵高出水面一百多英尺的巨大冰墙。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Suddenly, there was a slight trembling sound from below, and the captain went down to see what had happened.
rows.zh: 突然，船底下传来轻微的颤动声，船长便下去查看出了什么事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The noise had been so faint that no one thought that the ship had been damaged.
rows.zh: 那声音微弱得没有人想到船已经受损。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Below, the captain realized to his horror that the Titanic was sinking rapidly, for five of her sixteen watertight compartments had already been flooded!
rows.zh: 到了船舱下面，船长惊恐地发现，“泰坦尼克号”正在迅速下沉，因为十六个水密舱中已有五个进水了！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The order to abandon ship was given and hundreds of people plunged into the icy water.
rows.zh: 弃船的命令下达后，数百人跳进了冰冷的海水。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As there were not enough lifeboats for everybody, 1,500 lives were lost.
rows.zh: 由于救生艇不够全体人员使用，一千五百人丧生了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Customs Officers are quite tolerant these days, but they can still stop you when you are going through the Green Channel and have nothing to declare.
rows.zh: 如今海关人员相当宽容，不过即使你走绿色通道、没有需要申报的物品，他们仍可能拦住你。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even really honest people are often made to feel guilty.
rows.zh: 就连真正诚实的人，也常被弄得觉得自己像做了错事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The hardened professional smuggler, on the other hand, is never troubled by such feelings, even if he has five hundred gold watches hidden in his suitcase.
rows.zh: 反倒是老练的职业走私者，从不受这种感觉困扰，哪怕手提箱里藏着五百只金表也是如此。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When I returned from abroad recently, a particularly officious young Customs Officer clearly regarded me as a smuggler.
rows.zh: 最近我从国外回来时，一名格外爱摆官架子的年轻海关人员，显然把我当成了走私者。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: ‘Have you anything to declare?’ he asked, looking me in the eye.
rows.zh: “你有什么物品要申报吗？”他直视着我的眼睛问。
rows.speaker: 年轻海关人员

rows.en: ‘No,’ I answered confidently.
rows.zh: “没有，”我自信地回答。
rows.speaker: 我

rows.en: ‘Would you mind unlocking this suitcase please?’
rows.zh: “请把这只手提箱打开，可以吗？”
rows.speaker: 年轻海关人员

rows.en: ‘Not at all,’ I answered.
rows.zh: “当然可以，”我答道。
rows.speaker: 我

rows.en: The Officer went through the case with great care.
rows.zh: 那位海关人员十分仔细地检查了箱子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All the things I had packed so carefully were soon in a dreadful mess.
rows.zh: 我原本精心收好的东西，很快就被翻得乱七八糟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I felt sure I would never be able to close the case again.
rows.zh: 我确信自己再也没法把箱子合上了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Suddenly, I saw the Officer's face light up.
rows.zh: 突然，我看见那位海关人员脸上露出了喜色。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He had spotted a tiny bottle at the bottom of my case and he pounced on it with delight.
rows.zh: 他发现箱子底部有一个小瓶子，便高兴地一把抓住它。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: ‘Perfume, eh?’ he asked sarcastically.
rows.zh: “香水，嗯？”他讥讽地问。
rows.speaker: 年轻海关人员

rows.en: ‘You should have declared that.
rows.zh: “这东西你本来应该申报。
rows.speaker: 年轻海关人员

rows.en: Perfume is not exempt from import duty.’
rows.zh: 香水可不能免交进口税。”
rows.speaker: 年轻海关人员

rows.en: ‘But it isn’t perfume,’ I said.
rows.zh: “可这不是香水，”我说。
rows.speaker: 我

rows.en: ‘It’s hair gel.’ Then I added with a smile, ‘It’s a strange mixture I make myself.’
rows.zh: “这是发胶。”随后我又笑着补充说：“是我自己调配的一种奇特混合物。”
rows.speaker: 我

rows.en: As I expected, he did not believe me.
rows.zh: 正如我所料，他并不相信我的话。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: ‘Try it!’ I said encouragingly.
rows.zh: “试试看！”我鼓励他说。
rows.speaker: 我

rows.en: The Officer unscrewed the cap and put the bottle to his nostrils.
rows.zh: 那位海关人员拧开瓶盖，把瓶子凑到鼻孔前。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He was greeted by an unpleasant smell which convinced him that I was telling the truth.
rows.zh: 一股难闻的气味扑鼻而来，使他相信我说的是实话。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A few minutes later, I was able to hurry away with precious chalk marks on my baggage.
rows.zh: 几分钟后，我的行李上有了那宝贵的粉笔放行记号，我得以匆匆离开。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Most of us have formed an unrealistic picture of life on a desert island.
rows.zh: 我们大多数人对荒岛生活形成了一种不切实际的想象。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We sometimes imagine a desert island to be a sort of paradise where the sun always shines.
rows.zh: 有时，我们把荒岛想象成某种阳光永远普照的乐园。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Life there is simple and good.
rows.zh: 那里的生活简单又美好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Ripe fruit falls from the trees and you never have to work.
rows.zh: 成熟的果实从树上掉下来，人根本不用干活。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The other side of the picture is quite the opposite.
rows.zh: 另一种想象则完全相反。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Life on a desert island is wretched.
rows.zh: 荒岛上的生活凄苦不堪。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You either starve to death or live like Robinson Crusoe, waiting for a boat which never comes.
rows.zh: 你要么饿死，要么像鲁滨孙·克鲁索那样生活，苦等一艘永远不会出现的船。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Perhaps there is an element of truth in both these pictures, but few of us have had the opportunity to find out.
rows.zh: 这两种想象也许都多少有些道理，但我们中很少有人有机会去验证。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Two men who recently spent five days on a coral island wished they had stayed there longer.
rows.zh: 最近，有两个人在一座珊瑚岛上待了五天，他们却希望当时能在那儿多待些日子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They were taking a badly damaged boat from the Virgin Islands to Miami to have it repaired.
rows.zh: 他们正把一艘严重受损的船从维尔京群岛开往迈阿密去修理。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: During the journey, their boat began to sink.
rows.zh: 途中，他们的船开始下沉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They quickly loaded a small rubber dinghy with food, matches, and cans of beer and rowed for a few miles across the Caribbean until they arrived at a tiny coral island.
rows.zh: 他们迅速把食物、火柴和罐装啤酒装进一只小橡皮艇，在加勒比海上划了几英里，来到一座小小的珊瑚岛。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There were hardly any trees on the island and there was no water, but this did not prove to be a problem.
rows.zh: 岛上几乎没有树，也没有水，但事实证明，这并未成为问题。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The men collected rainwater in the rubber dinghy.
rows.zh: 他们用橡皮艇收集雨水。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As they had brought a spear gun with them, they had plenty to eat.
rows.zh: 由于带了鱼枪，他们有充足的食物。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They caught lobster and fish every day, and, as one of them put it ‘ate like kings’.
rows.zh: 他们每天捕龙虾和鱼，用其中一人的话说，吃得“像国王一样”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When a passing tanker rescued them five days later, both men were genuinely sorry that they had to leave.
rows.zh: 五天后，一艘路过的油轮救起了他们，两人对不得不离开这里都真心感到遗憾。
rows.speaker: 旁白
