rows.en: After her husband had gone to work, Mrs. Richards sent her children to school and went upstairs to her bedroom.
rows.zh: 丈夫上班后，理查兹太太送孩子们去上学，随后上楼进了自己的卧室。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She was too excited to do any housework that morning, for in the evening she would be going to a fancy-dress party with her husband.
rows.zh: 那天早晨，她兴奋得什么家务都做不下去，因为当晚她要和丈夫一起参加化装舞会。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She intended to dress up as a ghost and as she had made her costume the night before, she was impatient to try it on.
rows.zh: 她打算装扮成鬼；服装已在前一天晚上做好，她迫不及待地想试穿一下。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though the costume consisted only of a sheet, it was very effective.
rows.zh: 尽管这套服装只有一条床单，效果却很好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After putting it on, Mrs. Richards went downstairs.
rows.zh: 理查兹太太穿上它后，下了楼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She wanted to find out whether it would be comfortable to wear.
rows.zh: 她想看看穿着它是否舒服。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Just as Mrs. Richards was entering the dining room, there was a knock on the front door.
rows.zh: 理查兹太太刚要走进餐厅，前门就传来了敲门声。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She knew that it must be the baker.
rows.zh: 她知道，来的一定是送面包的人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She had told him to come straight in if ever she failed to open the door and to leave the bread on the kitchen table.
rows.zh: 她曾告诉他，如果有时她没来开门，就直接进来，把面包放在厨房桌上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Not wanting to frighten the poor man, Mrs. Richards quickly hid in the small storeroom under the stairs.
rows.zh: 理查兹太太不想吓着这可怜的人，便赶紧躲进楼梯下的小储藏室。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She heard the front door open and heavy footsteps in the hall.
rows.zh: 她听见前门开了，门厅里响起沉重的脚步声。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Suddenly the door of the storeroom was opened and a man entered.
rows.zh: 突然，储藏室的门打开了，一个男人走了进来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mrs. Richards realized that it must be the man from the Electricity Board who had come to read the meter.
rows.zh: 理查兹太太这才明白，来的一定是供电局查电表的人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She tried to explain the situation, saying ‘It’s only me’, but it was too late.
rows.zh: 她想解释情况，说“是我呀”，可已经太晚了。
rows.speaker: 理查兹太太

rows.en: The man let out a cry and jumped back several paces.
rows.zh: 那人惊叫一声，向后跳了好几步。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When Mrs. Richards walked towards him, he fled, slamming the door behind him.
rows.zh: 理查兹太太朝他走去时，他逃了出去，砰地关上了身后的门。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: dress up 表示穿特别服装，as 后说明扮演的角色。
usage.example: She intended to dress up as a ghost and as she had made her costume the night before, she was impatient to try it on.
usage.exampleZh: 她打算装扮成鬼；服装已在前一天晚上做好，她迫不及待地想试穿一下。

usage.note: 这里是急切期待，不是对人发脾气；try it on 中代词须放在 try 与 on 之间。
usage.example: She intended to dress up as a ghost and as she had made her costume the night before, she was impatient to try it on.
usage.exampleZh: 她打算装扮成鬼；服装已在前一天晚上做好，她迫不及待地想试穿一下。

usage.note: consist of 通常不用被动语态；本句 only 插在动词与 of 之间，强调服装只有一条床单。
usage.example: Though the costume consisted only of a sheet, it was very effective.
usage.exampleZh: 尽管这套服装只有一条床单，效果却很好。

usage.note: straight 在此为副词，表示不耽搁、不绕道，不能换成形容词 straight 的其他义项。
usage.example: She had told him to come straight in if ever she failed to open the door and to leave the bread on the kitchen table.
usage.exampleZh: 她曾告诉他，如果有时她没来开门，就直接进来，把面包放在厨房桌上。

usage.note: let out 可表示发出声音，如 let out a sigh；let 的过去式仍为 let。
usage.example: The man let out a cry and jumped back several paces.
usage.exampleZh: 那人惊叫一声，向后跳了好几步。

rows.en: There was a time when the owners of shops and businesses in Chicago had to pay large sums of money to gangsters in return for ‘protection’.
rows.zh: 曾经有一个时期，芝加哥的商店和企业主必须向黑帮缴纳大笔金钱，以换取所谓的“保护”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If the money was not paid promptly, the gangsters would quickly put a man out of business by destroying his shop.
rows.zh: 如果钱没及时交上，黑帮很快就会毁掉店铺，让店主无法继续营业。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Obtaining ‘protection money’ is not a modern crime.
rows.zh: 收取“保护费”并不是现代才出现的罪行。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As long ago as the fourteenth century, an Englishman, Sir John Hawkwood, made the remarkable discovery that people would rather pay large sums of money than have their life work destroyed by gangsters.
rows.zh: 早在十四世纪，英国人约翰·霍克伍德爵士就有了一个惊人的发现：人们宁可付出大笔金钱，也不愿让黑帮毁掉自己一生的心血。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Six hundred years ago, Sir John Hawkwood arrived in Italy with a band of soldiers and settled near Florence.
rows.zh: 六百年前，约翰·霍克伍德爵士带着一队士兵来到意大利，在佛罗伦萨附近驻扎下来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He soon made a name for himself and came to be known to the Italians as Giovanni Acuto.
rows.zh: 他很快闯出了名声，意大利人逐渐把他称为乔瓦尼·阿库托。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Whenever the Italian city-states were at war with each other, Hawkwood used to hire his soldiers to princes who were willing to pay the high price he demanded.
rows.zh: 每当意大利各城邦交战时，霍克伍德就把手下的士兵出租给愿意支付他所索高价的王公。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In times of peace, when business was bad, Hawkwood and his men would march into a city-state and, after burning down a few farms, would offer to go away if protection money was paid to them.
rows.zh: 和平时期生意清淡，霍克伍德和手下便开进某个城邦，烧掉几座农场，然后提出，只要付给他们保护费，他们就离开。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Hawkwood made large sums of money in this way.
rows.zh: 霍克伍德用这种办法赚到了大笔钱财。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In spite of this, the Italians regarded him as a sort of hero.
rows.zh: 尽管如此，意大利人却把他视为某种英雄。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When he died at the age of eighty, the Florentines gave him a state funeral and had a picture painted which was dedicated to the memory of ‘the most valiant soldier and most notable leader, Signor Giovanni Haukodue’.
rows.zh: 他八十岁去世时，佛罗伦萨人为他举行了国葬，并请人画了一幅画像，以纪念“最英勇的战士、最卓越的领袖乔瓦尼·霍科杜埃先生”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: for 后说明对方给予的事物；本课所谓保护实际是黑帮敲诈的名目。
usage.example: There was a time when the owners of shops and businesses in Chicago had to pay large sums of money to gangsters in return for ‘protection’.
usage.exampleZh: 曾经有一个时期，芝加哥的商店和企业主必须向黑帮缴纳大笔金钱，以换取所谓的“保护”。

usage.matchedForm: put a man out of business
usage.note: out of business 表示不再经营，不是因公外出。
usage.example: If the money was not paid promptly, the gangsters would quickly put a man out of business by destroying his shop.
usage.exampleZh: 如果钱没及时交上，黑帮很快就会毁掉店铺，让店主无法继续营业。

usage.note: 强调时间之久，与表示条件的 as long as 用法不同。
usage.example: As long ago as the fourteenth century, an Englishman, Sir John Hawkwood, made the remarkable discovery that people would rather pay large sums of money than have their life work destroyed by gangsters.
usage.exampleZh: 早在十四世纪，英国人约翰·霍克伍德爵士就有了一个惊人的发现：人们宁可付出大笔金钱，也不愿让黑帮毁掉自己一生的心血。

usage.note: 表示因成就、表现或活动而被人熟知，未必一定是好名声。
usage.example: He soon made a name for himself and came to be known to the Italians as Giovanni Acuto.
usage.exampleZh: 他很快闯出了名声，意大利人逐渐把他称为乔瓦尼·阿库托。

usage.note: of 后接名词、代词或动名词；若接完整从句，通常用 in spite of the fact that。
usage.example: In spite of this, the Italians regarded him as a sort of hero.
usage.exampleZh: 尽管如此，意大利人却把他视为某种英雄。

rows.en: Children always appreciate small gifts of money.
rows.zh: 孩子们总喜欢得到一点小额的零用钱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mum or dad, of course, provide a regular supply of pocket money, but uncles and aunts are always a source of extra income.
rows.zh: 当然，爸爸妈妈会定期给零花钱，但叔伯姑姨总是额外收入的来源。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: With some children, small sums go a long way.
rows.zh: 对有些孩子来说，一点钱也能花上很久。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If fifty pence pieces are not exchanged for sweets, they rattle for months inside money boxes.
rows.zh: 如果五十便士的硬币没有被拿去买糖果，就会在储蓄罐里叮当作响地待上几个月。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Only very thrifty children manage to fill up a money box.
rows.zh: 只有非常节俭的孩子才能把储蓄罐装满。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For most of them, fifty pence is a small price to pay for a nice big bar of chocolate.
rows.zh: 对大多数孩子来说，花五十便士买一大块好吃的巧克力，是很划算的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: My nephew, George, has a money box but it is always empty.
rows.zh: 我的侄子乔治有个储蓄罐，可里面总是空的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Very few of the fifty pence pieces and pound coins I have given him have found their way there.
rows.zh: 我给他的五十便士和一英镑硬币，几乎没几枚进过那个罐子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I gave him fifty pence yesterday and advised him to save it.
rows.zh: 昨天，我给了他五十便士，劝他存起来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Instead he bought himself fifty pence worth of trouble.
rows.zh: 可他却用这五十便士给自己买来了麻烦。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On his way to the sweet shop, he dropped his fifty pence and it bounced along the pavement and then disappeared down a drain.
rows.zh: 去糖果店的路上，他把五十便士硬币掉到了地上；硬币沿人行道弹跳着，接着落进排水沟，不见了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: George took off his jacket, rolled up his sleeves and pushed his right arm through the drain cover.
rows.zh: 乔治脱下外套，卷起袖子，把右胳膊伸进排水沟盖的缝隙。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He could not find his fifty pence piece anywhere, and what is more, he could not get his arm out.
rows.zh: 他怎么也找不到那枚五十便士硬币，而且更糟的是，他的胳膊也拔不出来了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A crowd of people gathered round him and a lady rubbed his arm with soap and butter, but George was firmly stuck.
rows.zh: 一群人围了过来，一位女士用肥皂和黄油涂抹他的胳膊，可乔治还是卡得紧紧的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The fire brigade was called and two fire fighters freed George using a special type of grease.
rows.zh: 有人叫来了消防队，两名消防员用一种特殊的润滑油脂，才把乔治解救出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: George was not too upset by his experience because the lady who owns the sweet shop heard about his troubles and rewarded him with a large box of chocolates.
rows.zh: 乔治倒没有因为这番经历太难过，因为糖果店的女店主听说他的麻烦后，奖给了他一大盒巧克力。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.meaning: 能用很久，能起很大作用
usage.note: 谈钱或物资时指少量也很经用、很有帮助，并非走很远的路。
usage.example: With some children, small sums go a long way.
usage.exampleZh: 对有些孩子来说，一点钱也能花上很久。

usage.note: up 强调达到满的状态；名词宾语可放后面，代词宾语须置于 fill 与 up 之间。
usage.example: Only very thrifty children manage to fill up a money box.
usage.exampleZh: 只有非常节俭的孩子才能把储蓄罐装满。

usage.note: 可用物作主语，表示物品辗转到达；本文否定语境说硬币几乎没有存进去。
usage.example: Very few of the fifty pence pieces and pound coins I have given him have found their way there.
usage.exampleZh: 我给他的五十便士和一英镑硬币，几乎没几枚进过那个罐子。

usage.note: 既可表示实际动作，也可比喻准备认真动手工作；本文是字面动作。
usage.example: George took off his jacket, rolled up his sleeves and pushed his right arm through the drain cover.
usage.exampleZh: 乔治脱下外套，卷起袖子，把右胳膊伸进排水沟盖的缝隙。

usage.note: 补充更进一步的信息；本课加入的是更糟糕的情况。
usage.example: He could not find his fifty pence piece anywhere, and what is more, he could not get his arm out.
usage.exampleZh: 他怎么也找不到那枚五十便士硬币，而且更糟的是，他的胳膊也拔不出来了。

rows.en: Mary and her husband Dimitri lived in the tiny village of Perachora in southern Greece.
rows.zh: 玛丽和丈夫迪米特里住在希腊南部的小村庄佩拉霍拉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One of Mary's prize possessions was a little white lamb which her husband had given her.
rows.zh: 玛丽最珍爱的东西之一，是丈夫送给她的一只小白羊。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She kept it tied to a tree in a field during the day and went to fetch it every evening.
rows.zh: 白天，她把小羊拴在田里的一棵树上，每天晚上再去把它牵回来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One evening, however, the lamb was missing.
rows.zh: 然而，一天傍晚，小羊不见了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The rope had been cut, so it was obvious that the lamb had been stolen.
rows.zh: 绳子被割断了，显然小羊是被人偷走的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When Dimitri came in from the fields, his wife told him what had happened.
rows.zh: 迪米特里从田里回来时，妻子把发生的事告诉了他。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Dimitri at once set out to find the thief.
rows.zh: 迪米特里立刻动身去找小偷。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He knew it would not prove difficult in such a small village.
rows.zh: 他知道，在这么小的村庄里，找到小偷不会太难。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After telling several of his friends about the theft, Dimitri found out that his neighbour, Aleko, had suddenly acquired a new lamb.
rows.zh: 迪米特里向几个朋友说起失窃的事后，得知邻居阿莱科突然多了一只新羊羔。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Dimitri immediately went to Aleko’s house and angrily accused him of stealing the lamb.
rows.zh: 迪米特里马上来到阿莱科家，愤怒地指责他偷了小羊。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He told him he had better return it or he would call the police.
rows.zh: 他告诉阿莱科，最好把羊还回来，否则他就报警。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Aleko denied taking it and led Dimitri into his backyard.
rows.zh: 阿莱科否认偷羊，领着迪米特里来到后院。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was true that he had just bought a lamb, he explained, but his lamb was black.
rows.zh: 他解释说，自己确实刚买了一只羊羔，不过他的羊是黑色的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Ashamed of having acted so rashly, Dimitri apologized to Aleko for having accused him.
rows.zh: 迪米特里为自己的鲁莽感到羞愧，因而为错怪阿莱科向他道歉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: While they were talking it began to rain and Dimitri stayed in Aleko’s house until the rain stopped.
rows.zh: 他们谈话时下起了雨，迪米特里就在阿莱科家待到雨停。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When he went outside half an hour later, he was astonished to find that the little black lamb was almost white.
rows.zh: 半小时后，他走到外面，惊讶地发现那只小黑羊几乎变成白色的了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Its wool, which had been dyed black, had been washed clean by the rain!
rows.zh: 原来，羊毛是染黑的，雨水已经把染料冲洗干净了！
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: prize 在此作定语，表示极珍贵、令人自豪，并非一定指获奖得到的物品。
usage.example: One of Mary's prize possessions was a little white lamb which her husband had given her.
usage.exampleZh: 玛丽最珍爱的东西之一，是丈夫送给她的一只小白羊。

usage.note: 后接动词原形，强调有明确目的地开始行动。
usage.example: Dimitri at once set out to find the thief.
usage.exampleZh: 迪米特里立刻动身去找小偷。

usage.meaning: 指控或指责某人做了某事
usage.note: of 后接名词或动名词；不要与 blame somebody for 的介词混淆。
usage.example: Dimitri immediately went to Aleko’s house and angrily accused him of stealing the lamb.
usage.exampleZh: 迪米特里马上来到阿莱科家，愤怒地指责他偷了小羊。

usage.note: 后接动词原形，常包含劝告或警告意味；否定为 had better not do。
usage.example: He told him he had better return it or he would call the police.
usage.exampleZh: 他告诉阿莱科，最好把羊还回来，否则他就报警。

usage.note: to 引出道歉对象，for 引出原因；having done 强调行为先于道歉发生。
usage.example: Ashamed of having acted so rashly, Dimitri apologized to Aleko for having accused him.
usage.exampleZh: 迪米特里为自己的鲁莽感到羞愧，因而为错怪阿莱科向他道歉。

lessons.title: The longest suspension bridge in the world

rows.en: Verrazano, an Italian about whom little is known, sailed into New York Harbour in 1524 and named it Angoulême.
rows.zh: 一五二四年，一位名叫韦拉扎诺、身世鲜为人知的意大利人驶入纽约港，并把它命名为昂古莱姆。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He described it as ‘a very agreeable situation located within two small hills in the midst of which flowed a great river.’
rows.zh: 他把这里描述为“一个十分宜人的地方，位于两座小山之间，一条大河从中流过”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though Verrazano is by no means considered to be a great explorer, his name will probably remain immortal, for on November 21st, 1964, the longest suspension bridge in the world was named after him.
rows.zh: 尽管韦拉扎诺绝不能算作伟大的探险家，他的名字却可能永垂不朽，因为一九六四年十一月二十一日，当时世界上最长的悬索桥以他的名字命名。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Verrazano Bridge, which was designed by Othmar Ammann, joins Brooklyn to Staten Island.
rows.zh: 韦拉扎诺大桥由奥特马尔·阿曼设计，连接布鲁克林和斯塔滕岛。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It has a span of 4,260 feet.
rows.zh: 它的跨度为四千二百六十英尺。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The bridge is so long that the shape of the earth had to be taken into account by its designer.
rows.zh: 桥身长到设计者不得不把地球的形状考虑在内。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Two great towers support four huge cables.
rows.zh: 两座巨塔支撑着四根巨大的钢缆。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The towers are built on immense underwater platforms made of steel and concrete.
rows.zh: 桥塔建在巨大的水下平台上，平台由钢材和混凝土建成。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The platforms extend to a depth of over 100 feet under the sea.
rows.zh: 这些平台伸至海面下一百多英尺的深处。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These alone took sixteen months to build.
rows.zh: 仅建造这些平台就花了十六个月。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Above the surface of the water, the towers rise to a height of nearly 700 feet.
rows.zh: 桥塔在水面以上高耸近七百英尺。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They support the cables from which the bridge has been suspended.
rows.zh: 它们支撑着钢缆，桥身就悬吊在这些钢缆上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Each of the four cables contains 26,108 lengths of wire.
rows.zh: 四根钢缆中的每一根都包含两万六千一百零八根钢丝。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It has been estimated that if the bridge were packed with cars, it would still only be carrying a third of its total capacity.
rows.zh: 据估计，即使桥上挤满汽车，承受的重量也仅为其总承载能力的三分之一。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: However, size and strength are not the only important things about this bridge.
rows.zh: 不过，规模和强度并不是这座桥仅有的重要特点。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Despite its immensity, it is both simple and elegant, fulfilling its designer’s dream to create ‘an enormous object drawn as faintly as possible’.
rows.zh: 它虽然庞大，却既简洁又优美，实现了设计者的梦想：创造“一个用尽可能轻淡的线条勾勒出来的庞然大物”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 语气强烈的否定；若放在句首修饰整句，通常需用部分倒装。
usage.example: Though Verrazano is by no means considered to be a great explorer, his name will probably remain immortal, for on November 21st, 1964, the longest suspension bridge in the world was named after him.
usage.exampleZh: 尽管韦拉扎诺绝不能算作伟大的探险家，他的名字却可能永垂不朽，因为一九六四年十一月二十一日，当时世界上最长的悬索桥以他的名字命名。

usage.note: be named after somebody 表示名称取自某人，以示纪念或关联。
usage.example: Though Verrazano is by no means considered to be a great explorer, his name will probably remain immortal, for on November 21st, 1964, the longest suspension bridge in the world was named after him.
usage.exampleZh: 尽管韦拉扎诺绝不能算作伟大的探险家，他的名字却可能永垂不朽，因为一九六四年十一月二十一日，当时世界上最长的悬索桥以他的名字命名。

usage.note: 宾语可置于 take 与 into account 之间；被动形式为 be taken into account。
usage.example: The bridge is so long that the shape of the earth had to be taken into account by its designer.
usage.exampleZh: 桥身长到设计者不得不把地球的形状考虑在内。

usage.note: depth 为深度；描述向下延伸时，to 表示达到的限度。
usage.example: The platforms extend to a depth of over 100 feet under the sea.
usage.exampleZh: 这些平台伸至海面下一百多英尺的深处。

usage.note: packed 强调密集；本句 were 与 would 配合，表达假设条件。
usage.example: It has been estimated that if the bridge were packed with cars, it would still only be carrying a third of its total capacity.
usage.exampleZh: 据估计，即使桥上挤满汽车，承受的重量也仅为其总承载能力的三分之一。

rows.en: Modern sculpture rarely surprises us any more.
rows.zh: 现代雕塑已很少再让我们惊讶了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The idea that modern art can only be seen in museums is mistaken.
rows.zh: 认为只有在博物馆里才能见到现代艺术，这种看法是错误的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even people who take no interest in art cannot have failed to notice examples of modern sculpture on display in public places.
rows.zh: 即使对艺术毫无兴趣的人，也不可能没有注意到公共场所陈列的现代雕塑作品。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Strange forms stand in gardens, and outside buildings and shops.
rows.zh: 花园里、建筑物和商店外，到处矗立着奇形怪状的造型。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We have got quite used to them.
rows.zh: 我们已经相当习惯它们了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Some so-called ‘modern’ pieces have been on display for nearly eighty years.
rows.zh: 有些所谓的“现代”作品，已经展出将近八十年了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In spite of this, some people—including myself—were surprised by a recent exhibition of modern sculpture.
rows.zh: 尽管如此，最近的一次现代雕塑展还是使一些人——包括我在内——感到意外。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The first thing I saw when I entered the art gallery was a notice which said: ‘Do not touch the exhibits.
rows.zh: 我一走进美术馆，首先看到的是一块告示，上面写着：“请勿触摸展品。
rows.speaker: 展览告示

rows.en: Some of them are dangerous!’
rows.zh: 其中一些有危险！”
rows.speaker: 展览告示

rows.en: The objects on display were pieces of moving sculpture.
rows.zh: 展出的都是些能够运动的雕塑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Oddly shaped forms that are suspended from the ceiling and move in response to a gust of wind are quite familiar to everybody.
rows.zh: 那些吊在天花板上、随一阵风而动的奇特造型，大家都很熟悉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These objects, however, were different.
rows.zh: 可是，这些展品却不同。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Lined up against the wall, there were long thin wires attached to metal spheres.
rows.zh: 沿着墙排列着一些细长的金属线，线上连着金属球。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The spheres had been magnetized and attracted or repelled each other all the time.
rows.zh: 这些球已经磁化，始终在彼此吸引或排斥。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the centre of the hall, there were a number of tall structures which contained coloured lights.
rows.zh: 大厅中央有一些高大的构架，里面装着彩灯。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These lights flickered continuously like traffic lights which have gone mad.
rows.zh: 这些灯不停地闪烁，像发了疯的交通信号灯。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Sparks were emitted from small black boxes and red lamps flashed on and off angrily.
rows.zh: 小黑盒子里迸出火花，红灯气势汹汹地忽明忽灭。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was rather like an exhibition of prehistoric electronic equipment.
rows.zh: 这倒很像一场史前电子设备展览。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These peculiar forms not only seemed designed to shock people emotionally, but to give them electric shocks as well!
rows.zh: 这些奇特的造型，似乎不仅是为了在情感上震撼人们，还要给人实实在在的电击！
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: interest 前可加 an、little 或 no 等；本句 no 表示毫无兴趣。
usage.example: Even people who take no interest in art cannot have failed to notice examples of modern sculpture on display in public places.
usage.exampleZh: 即使对艺术毫无兴趣的人，也不可能没有注意到公共场所陈列的现代雕塑作品。

usage.note: 常作表语或后置定语；也可说 be on display。
usage.example: Even people who take no interest in art cannot have failed to notice examples of modern sculpture on display in public places.
usage.exampleZh: 即使对艺术毫无兴趣的人，也不可能没有注意到公共场所陈列的现代雕塑作品。

usage.note: to 为介词，后接名词、代词或动名词；get 强调逐渐适应的过程。
usage.example: We have got quite used to them.
usage.exampleZh: 我们已经相当习惯它们了。

usage.note: 既可用于对问题作出回应，也可描述事物受外界刺激而变化。
usage.example: Oddly shaped forms that are suspended from the ceiling and move in response to a gust of wind are quite familiar to everybody.
usage.exampleZh: 那些吊在天花板上、随一阵风而动的奇特造型，大家都很熟悉。

usage.note: 在本句修饰 flash，表示灯反复亮灭；也可指某活动断断续续。
usage.example: Sparks were emitted from small black boxes and red lamps flashed on and off angrily.
usage.exampleZh: 小黑盒子里迸出火花，红灯气势汹汹地忽明忽灭。

rows.en: Kidnappers are rarely interested in animals, but they recently took considerable interest in Mrs. Eleanor Ramsay’s cat.
rows.zh: 绑架者很少对动物感兴趣，可最近他们却对埃莉诺·拉姆齐太太的猫产生了浓厚兴趣。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mrs. Eleanor Ramsay, a very wealthy old lady, has shared a flat with her cat, Rastus, for a great many years.
rows.zh: 埃莉诺·拉姆齐太太是位十分富有的老太太，多年来一直和她的猫拉斯特斯同住一套公寓。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Rastus leads an orderly life.
rows.zh: 拉斯特斯的生活很有规律。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He usually takes a short walk in the evenings and is always home by seven o’clock.
rows.zh: 他通常傍晚出去散步一小会儿，最迟七点就会回到家。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One evening, however, he failed to arrive.
rows.zh: 然而，有一天晚上，他没有回来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mrs. Ramsay got very worried.
rows.zh: 拉姆齐太太十分担心。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She looked everywhere for him but could not find him.
rows.zh: 她到处寻找，却怎么也找不到他。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Three days after Rastus’ disappearance, Mrs. Ramsay received an anonymous letter.
rows.zh: 拉斯特斯失踪三天后，拉姆齐太太收到了一封匿名信。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The writer stated that Rastus was in safe hands and would be returned immediately if Mrs. Ramsay paid a ransom of £1,000.
rows.zh: 写信的人声称，拉斯特斯正受到妥善照顾，只要拉姆齐太太付一千英镑赎金，就马上把他送回来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mrs. Ramsay was instructed to place the money in a cardboard box and to leave it outside her door.
rows.zh: 信中要求拉姆齐太太把钱放进一个纸板盒，留在自家门外。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At first, she decided to go to the police, but fearing that she would never see Rastus again—the letter had made that quite clear—she changed her mind.
rows.zh: 起初，她决定去报警，可又担心再也见不到拉斯特斯——信里已把这一点说得很清楚——于是改变了主意。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She withdrew £1,000 from her bank and followed the kidnapper’s instructions.
rows.zh: 她从银行取出一千英镑，照绑架者的指示做了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The next morning, the box had disappeared but Mrs. Ramsay was sure that the kidnapper would keep his word.
rows.zh: 第二天早晨，盒子不见了，但拉姆齐太太相信绑架者会信守诺言。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Sure enough, Rastus arrived punctually at seven o'clock that evening.
rows.zh: 果然，那天晚上七点，拉斯特斯准时回来了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He looked very well, though he was rather thirsty, for he drank half a bottle of milk.
rows.zh: 他看起来很好，不过相当口渴，因为他喝了半瓶牛奶。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The police were astounded when Mrs. Ramsay told them what she had done.
rows.zh: 拉姆齐太太把自己的做法告诉警方时，警察们大为震惊。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She explained that Rastus was very dear to her.
rows.zh: 她解释说，拉斯特斯对她而言非常珍贵。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Considering the amount she paid, he was dear in more ways than one!
rows.zh: 想想她付出的那笔钱，他的“贵”可不止一层意思！
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 后接可数名词复数；若接不可数名词，通常用 a great deal of。
usage.example: Mrs. Eleanor Ramsay, a very wealthy old lady, has shared a flat with her cat, Rastus, for a great many years.
usage.exampleZh: 埃莉诺·拉姆齐太太是位十分富有的老太太，多年来一直和她的猫拉斯特斯同住一套公寓。

usage.note: lead a ... life 表示过着某种生活，形容词用于说明生活状态。
usage.example: Rastus leads an orderly life.
usage.exampleZh: 拉斯特斯的生活很有规律。

usage.note: 强调由可信赖的人照管；本句只是匿名信中的声称。
usage.example: The writer stated that Rastus was in safe hands and would be returned immediately if Mrs. Ramsay paid a ransom of £1,000.
usage.exampleZh: 写信的人声称，拉斯特斯正受到妥善照顾，只要拉姆齐太太付一千英镑赎金，就马上把他送回来。

usage.note: word 在此指承诺，通常用单数，不说 keep one’s words 表达同一习语。
usage.example: The next morning, the box had disappeared but Mrs. Ramsay was sure that the kidnapper would keep his word.
usage.exampleZh: 第二天早晨，盒子不见了，但拉姆齐太太相信绑架者会信守诺言。

usage.note: 用来引出实际发生且印证此前预期的结果。
usage.example: Sure enough, Rastus arrived punctually at seven o'clock that evening.
usage.exampleZh: 果然，那天晚上七点，拉斯特斯准时回来了。

usage.note: 本课利用 dear 的双关，既指珍爱，也指花费昂贵。
usage.example: Considering the amount she paid, he was dear in more ways than one!
usage.exampleZh: 想想她付出的那笔钱，他的“贵”可不止一层意思！

rows.en: In 1908 Lord Northcliffe offered a prize of £1,000 to the first man who would fly across the English Channel.
rows.zh: 一九〇八年，诺思克利夫勋爵悬赏一千英镑，奖给第一个驾机飞越英吉利海峡的人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Over a year passed before the first attempt was made.
rows.zh: 一年多过去后，才有人进行首次尝试。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On July 19th, 1909, in the early morning, Hubert Latham took off from the French coast in his plane the ‘Antoinette IV’.
rows.zh: 一九〇九年七月十九日清晨，休伯特·莱瑟姆驾驶“安托瓦内特四号”飞机从法国海岸起飞。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He had travelled only seven miles across the Channel when his engine failed and he was forced to land on the sea.
rows.zh: 他在海峡上空才飞了七英里，发动机就出了故障，被迫在海上降落。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The ‘Antoinette’ floated on the water until Latham was picked up by a ship.
rows.zh: “安托瓦内特号”一直浮在水面上，直到一艘船把莱瑟姆救起。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Two days later, Louis Bleriot arrived near Calais with a plane called ‘No. XI’.
rows.zh: 两天后，路易·布莱里奥带着一架名叫“十一号”的飞机，来到加来附近。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Bleriot had been making planes since 1905 and this was his latest model.
rows.zh: 布莱里奥从一九〇五年起就一直制造飞机，这架是他的最新机型。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A week before, he had completed a successful overland flight during which he covered twenty-six miles.
rows.zh: 一周前，他成功完成了一次陆上飞行，飞越了二十六英里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Latham, however, did not give up easily.
rows.zh: 然而，莱瑟姆并没有轻易放弃。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He, too, arrived near Calais on the same day with a new ‘Antoinette’.
rows.zh: 同一天，他也带着一架新的“安托瓦内特号”来到加来附近。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It looked as if there would be an exciting race across the Channel.
rows.zh: 看来，一场激动人心的飞越海峡比赛即将展开。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Both planes were going to take off on July 25th, but Latham failed to get up early enough.
rows.zh: 两架飞机原定七月二十五日起飞，但莱瑟姆没能起得足够早。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After making a short test flight at 4.15 a.m., Bleriot set off half an hour later.
rows.zh: 凌晨四点十五分，布莱里奥作了一次短暂试飞，半小时后正式出发。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: His great flight lasted thirty-seven minutes.
rows.zh: 他这次伟大的飞行持续了三十七分钟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When he landed near Dover, the first person to greet him was a local policeman.
rows.zh: 他在多佛附近降落时，第一个前来迎接他的人是一名当地警察。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Latham made another attempt a week later and got within half a mile of Dover, but he was unlucky again.
rows.zh: 一周后，莱瑟姆再次尝试，飞到了距离多佛不到半英里的地方，可他又一次遭遇了不幸。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: His engine failed and he landed on the sea for the second time.
rows.zh: 他的发动机出了故障，第二次降落在海上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 用于飞机离开地面；还可表示脱下衣物，需根据宾语和语境区分。
usage.example: On July 19th, 1909, in the early morning, Hubert Latham took off from the French coast in his plane the ‘Antoinette IV’.
usage.exampleZh: 一九〇九年七月十九日清晨，休伯特·莱瑟姆驾驶“安托瓦内特四号”飞机从法国海岸起飞。

usage.note: 表示情势或外力使人不得不行动，后接动词原形。
usage.example: He had travelled only seven miles across the Channel when his engine failed and he was forced to land on the sea.
usage.exampleZh: 他在海峡上空才飞了七英里，发动机就出了故障，被迫在海上降落。

usage.note: 本句指船从水中救人；被动语态下救助者由 by 引出。
usage.example: The ‘Antoinette’ floated on the water until Latham was picked up by a ship.
usage.exampleZh: “安托瓦内特号”一直浮在水面上，直到一艘船把莱瑟姆救起。

usage.note: 可单独使用，也可后接名词或动名词；不直接接 to do 表示停止做某事。
usage.example: Latham, however, did not give up easily.
usage.exampleZh: 然而，莱瑟姆并没有轻易放弃。

usage.note: as if 引导表语从句，可根据真实可能性使用相应时态。
usage.example: It looked as if there would be an exciting race across the Channel.
usage.exampleZh: 看来，一场激动人心的飞越海峡比赛即将展开。

rows.en: Boxing matches were very popular in England two hundred years ago.
rows.zh: 两百年前，拳击比赛在英国很受欢迎。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In those days, boxers fought with bare fists for prize money.
rows.zh: 那时，拳手们赤手空拳地比赛，以争取奖金。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Because of this, they were known as ‘prizefighters’.
rows.zh: 因此，他们被称为“职业奖金拳手”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: However, boxing was very crude, for there were no rules and a prizefighter could be seriously injured or even killed during a match.
rows.zh: 不过，当时的拳击十分野蛮，因为没有规则，拳手在比赛中可能严重受伤，甚至丧命。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One of the most colourful figures in boxing history was Daniel Mendoza, who was born in 1764.
rows.zh: 拳击史上最富传奇色彩的人物之一，是生于一七六四年的丹尼尔·门多萨。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860, when the Marquis of Queensberry drew up the first set of rules.
rows.zh: 直到一八六〇年，昆斯伯里侯爵拟定第一套规则时，拳击才开始采用拳套。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though he was technically a prizefighter, Mendoza did much to change crude prizefighting into a sport, for he brought science to the game.
rows.zh: 严格说来，门多萨也是一名以奖金为生的拳手，但他把科学方法引入拳击，为把野蛮的职业拳赛变成一项体育运动作出了很大贡献。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In his day, Mendoza enjoyed tremendous popularity.
rows.zh: 在他那个时代，门多萨极受欢迎。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He was adored by rich and poor alike.
rows.zh: 无论贫富，人们都很崇拜他。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mendoza rose to fame swiftly after a boxing match when he was only fourteen years old.
rows.zh: 门多萨年仅十四岁时，在一场拳击比赛后迅速成名。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This attracted the attention of Richard Humphries who was then the most eminent boxer in England.
rows.zh: 这引起了理查德·汉弗莱斯的注意，他当时是英国最杰出的拳手。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He offered to train Mendoza and his young pupil was quick to learn.
rows.zh: 他提出训练门多萨，而这名年轻弟子学得很快。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In fact, Mendoza soon became so successful that Humphries turned against him.
rows.zh: 事实上，门多萨很快就大获成功，以至汉弗莱斯反而与他为敌。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The two men quarrelled bitterly and it was clear that the argument could only be settled by a fight.
rows.zh: 两人激烈争吵，显然这场争执只能靠打一场来解决。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A match was held at Stilton, where both men fought for an hour.
rows.zh: 比赛在斯蒂尔顿举行，两人打了一个小时。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The public bet a great deal of money on Mendoza, but he was defeated.
rows.zh: 公众把大笔赌注押在门多萨身上，可他却输了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mendoza met Humphries in the ring on a later occasion and he lost for a second time.
rows.zh: 后来，门多萨又一次在拳台上迎战汉弗莱斯，第二次落败。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was not until his third match in 1790 that he finally beat Humphries and became Champion of England.
rows.zh: 直到一七九〇年的第三次交手，他才终于击败汉弗莱斯，成为英国拳击冠军。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Meanwhile, he founded a highly successful Academy and even Lord Byron became one of his pupils.
rows.zh: 与此同时，他创办了一所极为成功的拳击学校，就连拜伦勋爵也成了他的学生。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He earned enormous sums of money and was paid as much as £100 for a single appearance.
rows.zh: 他赚了大笔钱财，单次出场的报酬就高达一百英镑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Despite this, he was so extravagant that he was always in debt.
rows.zh: 尽管如此，他挥霍无度，始终债台高筑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After he was defeated by a boxer called Gentleman Jackson, he was quickly forgotten.
rows.zh: 被一个叫“绅士杰克逊”的拳手击败后，他很快就被人遗忘了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He was sent to prison for failing to pay his debts and died in poverty in 1836.
rows.zh: 他因无力偿还债务而入狱，一八三六年在贫困中死去。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: bare 表示没有遮盖，fists 指拳头；文中与后来使用拳套相对。
usage.example: In those days, boxers fought with bare fists for prize money.
usage.exampleZh: 那时，拳手们赤手空拳地比赛，以争取奖金。

usage.note: 常用于规则、合同、计划等正式文件，过去式 draw 变为 drew。
usage.example: The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860, when the Marquis of Queensberry drew up the first set of rules.
usage.exampleZh: 直到一八六〇年，昆斯伯里侯爵拟定第一套规则时，拳击才开始采用拳套。

usage.note: rise 在这里是不及物动词，过去式为 rose，不要与及物动词 raise 混用。
usage.example: Mendoza rose to fame swiftly after a boxing match when he was only fourteen years old.
usage.exampleZh: 门多萨年仅十四岁时，在一场拳击比赛后迅速成名。

usage.note: 表示态度由支持或友好转为敌对，against 后接对象。
usage.example: In fact, Mendoza soon became so successful that Humphries turned against him.
usage.exampleZh: 事实上，门多萨很快就大获成功，以至汉弗莱斯反而与他为敌。

usage.note: be in debt 表示欠债状态，get into debt 强调开始负债。
usage.example: Despite this, he was so extravagant that he was always in debt.
usage.exampleZh: 尽管如此，他挥霍无度，始终债台高筑。

usage.note: poverty 为不可数名词；die in poverty 指在贫困中死去。
usage.example: He was sent to prison for failing to pay his debts and died in poverty in 1836.
usage.exampleZh: 他因无力偿还债务而入狱，一八三六年在贫困中死去。

rows.en: Some plays are so successful that they run for years on end.
rows.zh: 有些戏剧十分成功，连演多年不衰。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In many ways, this is unfortunate for the poor actors who are required to go on repeating the same lines night after night.
rows.zh: 从许多方面看，这对可怜的演员们并不幸运，因为他们得一夜又一夜地不断重复同样的台词。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One would expect them to know their parts by heart and never have cause to falter.
rows.zh: 按理说，人们会以为他们早已把自己的戏份背得滚瓜烂熟，绝不会有说不下去的时候。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Yet this is not always the case.
rows.zh: 然而，情况并非总是如此。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A famous actor in a highly successful play was once cast in the role of an aristocrat who had been imprisoned in the Bastille for twenty years.
rows.zh: 有一次，在一部极受欢迎的戏里，一位名演员被选中扮演一名在巴士底狱关押了二十年的贵族。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the last act, a gaoler would always come on to the stage with a letter which he would hand to the prisoner.
rows.zh: 到最后一幕，总有一个狱卒拿着一封信上台，把信交给囚犯。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even though the noble was expected to read the letter at each performance, he always insisted that it should be written out in full.
rows.zh: 虽然这位贵族每场演出都得读这封信，他却坚持要求把信的全文写出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One night, the gaoler decided to play a joke on his colleague to find out if, after so many performances, he had managed to learn the contents of the letter by heart.
rows.zh: 一天晚上，狱卒决定跟同事开个玩笑，看看演了这么多场以后，他究竟有没有把信的内容背下来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The curtain went up on the final act of the play and revealed the aristocrat sitting alone behind bars in his dark cell.
rows.zh: 最后一幕的帷幕拉开，观众看见贵族独自坐在昏暗牢房的铁栏后面。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Just then, the gaoler appeared with the precious letter in his hands.
rows.zh: 就在这时，狱卒手里拿着那封宝贵的信出现了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He entered the cell and presented the letter to the aristocrat.
rows.zh: 他走进牢房，把信递给贵族。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But the copy he gave him had not been written out in full as usual.
rows.zh: 可他这次交出的信，并没有像往常一样写出全文。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was simply a blank sheet of paper.
rows.zh: 那只是一张白纸。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The gaoler looked on eagerly, anxious to see if his fellow actor had at last learnt his lines.
rows.zh: 狱卒急切地在旁观看，想知道这位搭档到底有没有记住自己的台词。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The noble stared at the blank sheet of paper for a few seconds.
rows.zh: 贵族盯着白纸看了几秒钟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Then, squinting his eyes, he said: ‘The light is dim.
rows.zh: 接着，他眯起眼睛说：“光线太暗了。
rows.speaker: 扮演贵族的演员

rows.en: Read the letter to me.’
rows.zh: 把信念给我听。”
rows.speaker: 扮演贵族的演员

rows.en: And he promptly handed the sheet of paper to the gaoler.
rows.zh: 说着，他立即把那张纸递给了狱卒。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Finding that he could not remember a word of the letter either, the gaoler replied: ‘The light is indeed dim, sire.
rows.zh: 狱卒发现自己也记不起信里的一个字，便回答：“光线确实很暗，大人。
rows.speaker: 扮演狱卒的演员

rows.en: I must get my glasses.’
rows.zh: 我得去拿眼镜。”
rows.speaker: 扮演狱卒的演员

rows.en: With this, he hurried off the stage.
rows.zh: 说完，他匆匆离开了舞台。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Much to the aristocrat’s amusement, the gaoler returned a few moments later with a pair of glasses and the usual copy of the letter which he proceeded to read to the prisoner.
rows.zh: 让那位贵族大觉好笑的是，片刻后，狱卒拿着一副眼镜和往常那封信回来了，随即开始给囚犯念信。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: on end 表示连续不断地持续一段时间，前面常接 hours、days、years 等。
usage.example: Some plays are so successful that they run for years on end.
usage.exampleZh: 有些戏剧十分成功，连演多年不衰。

usage.note: learn 或 know something by heart 表示能够不看原文而记住或复述。
usage.example: One would expect them to know their parts by heart and never have cause to falter.
usage.exampleZh: 按理说，人们会以为他们早已把自己的戏份背得滚瓜烂熟，绝不会有说不下去的时候。

usage.note: the case 指实际情况，not always 是并非总是，并非完全否定。
usage.example: Yet this is not always the case.
usage.exampleZh: 然而，情况并非总是如此。

usage.note: 可用于文字、付款等，强调全部而无省略。
usage.example: Even though the noble was expected to read the letter at each performance, he always insisted that it should be written out in full.
usage.exampleZh: 虽然这位贵族每场演出都得读这封信，他却坚持要求把信的全文写出来。

usage.note: on 后接被戏弄的人；不说 play a joke to somebody。
usage.example: One night, the gaoler decided to play a joke on his colleague to find out if, after so many performances, he had managed to learn the contents of the letter by heart.
usage.exampleZh: 一天晚上，狱卒决定跟同事开个玩笑，看看演了这么多场以后，他究竟有没有把信的内容背下来。

usage.note: on 在此是副词；若要引出观看的事件，可另加介词结构。
usage.example: The gaoler looked on eagerly, anxious to see if his fellow actor had at last learnt his lines.
usage.exampleZh: 狱卒急切地在旁观看，想知道这位搭档到底有没有记住自己的台词。

lessons.title: One man’s meat is another man’s poison

rows.en: People become quite illogical when they try to decide what can be eaten and what cannot be eaten.
rows.zh: 人们一旦试着判断什么能吃、什么不能吃，就会变得十分不讲道理。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If you lived in the Mediterranean, for instance, you would consider octopus a great delicacy.
rows.zh: 例如，如果你生活在地中海地区，就会把章鱼视为一道美味佳肴。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You would not be able to understand why some people find it repulsive.
rows.zh: 你会无法理解，为什么有人会觉得它令人作呕。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On the other hand, your stomach would turn at the idea of frying potatoes in animal fat—the normally accepted practice in many northern countries.
rows.zh: 反过来，一想到用动物油脂炸土豆，你就会反胃，然而在许多北方国家，这却是通常被接受的做法。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The sad truth is that most of us have been brought up to eat certain foods and we stick to them all our lives.
rows.zh: 令人遗憾的事实是，我们大多数人从小被培养着吃某些食物，此后一辈子都不肯改变。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: No creature has received more praise and abuse than the common garden snail.
rows.zh: 没有哪种生物像常见的花园蜗牛这样，既受到如此多的赞美，又遭到如此多的嫌恶。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Cooked in wine, snails are a great luxury in various parts of the world.
rows.zh: 在世界上的许多地方，用葡萄酒烹制的蜗牛是一道奢侈佳肴。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There are countless people who, ever since their early years, have learned to associate snails with food.
rows.zh: 无数人从小就学会把蜗牛和食物联系起来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: My friend, Robert, lives in a country where snails are despised.
rows.zh: 我的朋友罗伯特住在一个人们厌恶蜗牛的国家。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As his flat is in a large town, he has no garden of his own.
rows.zh: 他的公寓位于一座大城市里，所以没有自己的花园。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For years he has been asking me to collect snails from my garden and take them to him.
rows.zh: 多年来，他一直请我从花园里捉些蜗牛带给他。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The idea never appealed to me very much, but one day, after a heavy shower, I happened to be walking in my garden when I noticed a huge number of snails taking a stroll on some of my prize plants.
rows.zh: 这个主意从来都不太吸引我；不过，有一天，一场大阵雨过后，我正好在花园里散步，发现许多蜗牛正悠然爬过我那些珍爱的花木。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Acting on a sudden impulse, I collected several dozen, put them in a paper bag, and took them to Robert.
rows.zh: 一时冲动之下，我捉了几十只，装进纸袋，带去给罗伯特。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Robert was delighted to see me and equally pleased with my little gift.
rows.zh: 罗伯特见到我非常高兴，对这份小礼物也同样喜欢。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I left the bag in the hall and Robert and I went into the living room where we talked for a couple of hours.
rows.zh: 我把纸袋放在门厅，然后和罗伯特进了客厅，在那里聊了几个小时。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I had forgotten all about the snails when Robert suddenly said that I must stay to dinner.
rows.zh: 我早把蜗牛忘得一干二净，这时罗伯特突然说，我一定得留下来吃晚饭。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Snails would, of course, be the main dish.
rows.zh: 当然，主菜会是蜗牛。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I did not fancy the idea and I reluctantly followed Robert out of the room.
rows.zh: 我并不喜欢这个主意，却还是不情愿地跟着罗伯特走出房间。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: To our dismay, we saw that there were snails everywhere: they had escaped from the paper bag and had taken complete possession of the hall!
rows.zh: 令我们沮丧的是，眼前到处都是蜗牛：它们从纸袋里逃了出来，把门厅完全占领了！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I have never been able to look at a snail since then.
rows.zh: 从那以后，我再也没法正眼看一只蜗牛了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: at 表示引起反应的原因，of 后接名词或动名词。
usage.example: On the other hand, your stomach would turn at the idea of frying potatoes in animal fat—the normally accepted practice in many northern countries.
usage.exampleZh: 反过来，一想到用动物油脂炸土豆，你就会反胃，然而在许多北方国家，这却是通常被接受的做法。

usage.note: to 是介词，后接所坚持的习惯、计划等；这里指不改变从小的饮食习惯。
usage.example: The sad truth is that most of us have been brought up to eat certain foods and we stick to them all our lives.
usage.exampleZh: 令人遗憾的事实是，我们大多数人从小被培养着吃某些食物，此后一辈子都不肯改变。

usage.note: associate A with B 表示在认识中建立两者的联系。
usage.example: There are countless people who, ever since their early years, have learned to associate snails with food.
usage.exampleZh: 无数人从小就学会把蜗牛和食物联系起来。

usage.note: 表示某事物对某人有吸引力，通常以事物为主语。
usage.example: The idea never appealed to me very much, but one day, after a heavy shower, I happened to be walking in my garden when I noticed a huge number of snails taking a stroll on some of my prize plants.
usage.exampleZh: 这个主意从来都不太吸引我；不过，有一天，一场大阵雨过后，我正好在花园里散步，发现许多蜗牛正悠然爬过我那些珍爱的花木。

usage.note: impulse 指未经充分思考的突然念头，on 表示受其驱动。
usage.example: Acting on a sudden impulse, I collected several dozen, put them in a paper bag, and took them to Robert.
usage.exampleZh: 一时冲动之下，我捉了几十只，装进纸袋，带去给罗伯特。

usage.note: possession 前可加 complete 等修饰词；本文把蜗牛写得像占领者，带幽默意味。
usage.example: To our dismay, we saw that there were snails everywhere: they had escaped from the paper bag and had taken complete possession of the hall!
usage.exampleZh: 令我们沮丧的是，眼前到处都是蜗牛：它们从纸袋里逃了出来，把门厅完全占领了！

rows.en: We often read in novels how a seemingly respectable person or family has some terrible secret which has been concealed from strangers for years.
rows.zh: 我们常在小说里读到：一个表面上体面的人或家庭，竟有一个多年来一直向外人隐瞒的可怕秘密。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The English language possesses a vivid saying to describe this sort of situation.
rows.zh: 英语里有一句生动的说法，用来形容这种情况。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The terrible secret is called ‘a skeleton in the cupboard’.
rows.zh: 这个可怕的秘密叫作“壁橱里的骷髅”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At some dramatic moment in the story, the terrible secret becomes known and a reputation is ruined.
rows.zh: 故事发展到某个戏剧性时刻，秘密被揭开，某个人的名声也就毁了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The reader’s hair stands on end when he reads in the final pages of the novel that the heroine, a dear old lady who had always been so kind to everybody, had, in her youth, poisoned every one of her five husbands.
rows.zh: 当读者在小说最后几页读到，那位始终对人人都很和善、令人喜爱的老太太主人公，年轻时竟把自己的五任丈夫一一毒死时，便会毛骨悚然。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is all very well for such things to occur in fiction.
rows.zh: 这种事发生在小说里倒也罢了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: To varying degrees, we all have secrets which we do not want even our closest friends to learn, but few of us have skeletons in the cupboard.
rows.zh: 我们每个人都多少有些连最亲密的朋友也不想让其知道的秘密，但真正藏有见不得人丑事的，却没有几个。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The only person I know who has a skeleton in the cupboard is George Carlton, and he is very proud of the fact.
rows.zh: 我认识的人里，唯一在壁橱里藏着骷髅的是乔治·卡尔顿，而且他对此颇为自豪。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: George studied medicine in his youth.
rows.zh: 乔治年轻时学过医。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Instead of becoming a doctor, however, he became a successful writer of detective stories.
rows.zh: 然而，他没有成为医生，倒成了一名成功的侦探小说作家。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I once spent an uncomfortable weekend which I shall never forget at his house.
rows.zh: 有一次，我在他家度过了一个令人不安、永生难忘的周末。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: George showed me to the guestroom which, he said, was rarely used.
rows.zh: 乔治领我去客房，说那间房很少使用。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He told me to unpack my things and then come down to dinner.
rows.zh: 他让我把东西拿出来放好，然后下楼吃晚饭。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After I had stacked my shirts and underclothes in two empty drawers, I decided to hang one of the two suits I had brought with me in the cupboard.
rows.zh: 我把衬衫和内衣叠放进两个空抽屉后，决定把随身带来的两套西装中的一套挂进壁橱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I opened the cupboard door and then stood in front of it petrified.
rows.zh: 我打开橱门，随后站在门前，吓得动弹不得。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A skeleton was dangling before my eyes.
rows.zh: 一具骷髅正吊在我眼前。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The sudden movement of the door made it sway slightly and it gave me the impression that it was about to leap out at me.
rows.zh: 猛然开门使它轻轻晃动，让我觉得它就要朝我扑出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Dropping my suit, I dashed downstairs to tell George.
rows.zh: 我扔下西装，冲到楼下去告诉乔治。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This was worse than ‘a terrible secret’; this was a real skeleton!
rows.zh: 这比“可怕的秘密”还要糟：这是一具真的骷髅！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But George was unsympathetic.
rows.zh: 可是，乔治却毫不体谅。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: ‘Oh, that,’ he said with a smile as if he were talking about an old friend.
rows.zh: “哦，那个呀，”他笑着说，好像在谈一位老朋友。
rows.speaker: 乔治·卡尔顿

rows.en: ‘That's Sebastian.
rows.zh: “那是塞巴斯蒂安。
rows.speaker: 乔治·卡尔顿

rows.en: You forget that I was a medical student once upon a time.’
rows.zh: 你忘了，我从前可是一名医学生。”
rows.speaker: 乔治·卡尔顿

usage.meaning: 不可告人的家丑或秘密
usage.note: 英国英语习语；美国英语也常说 a skeleton in the closet。本课后来又按字面写真的骷髅。
usage.example: The terrible secret is called ‘a skeleton in the cupboard’.
usage.exampleZh: 这个可怕的秘密叫作“壁橱里的骷髅”。

usage.note: 形容极度恐惧或惊骇，不必理解为头发真的全部竖起来。
usage.example: The reader’s hair stands on end when he reads in the final pages of the novel that the heroine, a dear old lady who had always been so kind to everybody, had, in her youth, poisoned every one of her five husbands.
usage.exampleZh: 当读者在小说最后几页读到，那位始终对人人都很和善、令人喜爱的老太太主人公，年轻时竟把自己的五任丈夫一一毒死时，便会毛骨悚然。

usage.note: 用于说明情况普遍存在，但各人或各事物的程度不一样。
usage.example: To varying degrees, we all have secrets which we do not want even our closest friends to learn, but few of us have skeletons in the cupboard.
usage.exampleZh: 我们每个人都多少有些连最亲密的朋友也不想让其知道的秘密，但真正藏有见不得人丑事的，却没有几个。

usage.note: 后接动词原形，强调眼看就要发生，不宜与明确的较远将来时间搭配。
usage.example: The sudden movement of the door made it sway slightly and it gave me the impression that it was about to leap out at me.
usage.exampleZh: 猛然开门使它轻轻晃动，让我觉得它就要朝我扑出来。

usage.note: 常见于故事开头，本文在谈话中诙谐地指自己当医学生的过去。
usage.example: You forget that I was a medical student once upon a time.’
usage.exampleZh: 你忘了，我从前可是一名医学生。”

rows.en: One of the most famous sailing ships of the nineteenth century, the Cutty Sark, can still be seen at Greenwich.
rows.zh: 十九世纪最著名的帆船之一“卡蒂萨克号”，如今仍可在格林尼治看到。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She stands on dry land and is visited by thousands of people each year.
rows.zh: 它安置在陆地上，每年有成千上万的人前来参观。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She serves as an impressive reminder of the great ships of the past.
rows.zh: 它让人们鲜明地想起昔日那些巨大的帆船。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Before they were replaced by steamships, sailing vessels like the Cutty Sark were used to carry tea from China and wool from Australia.
rows.zh: 在被蒸汽船取代以前，像“卡蒂萨克号”这样的帆船，曾被用来从中国运茶、从澳大利亚运羊毛。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Cutty Sark was one of the fastest sailing ships that has ever been built.
rows.zh: “卡蒂萨克号”是有史以来建造的最快的帆船之一。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The only other ship to match her was the Thermopylae.
rows.zh: 唯一能与它匹敌的船是“塞莫皮莱号”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Both these ships set out from Shanghai on June 18th, 1872 on an exciting race to England.
rows.zh: 一八七二年六月十八日，两艘船同时从上海出发，展开了一场驶往英国的激动人心的比赛。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This race, which went on for exactly four months, was the last of its kind.
rows.zh: 这场比赛整整持续了四个月，也是此类比赛的最后一次。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It marked the end of the great tradition of ships with sails and the beginning of a new era.
rows.zh: 它标志着伟大的帆船传统走向终结，一个新时代由此开始。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The first of the two ships to reach Java after the race had begun was the Thermopylae, but on the Indian Ocean, the Cutty Sark took the lead.
rows.zh: 比赛开始后，两艘船中先到爪哇的是“塞莫皮莱号”，但到了印度洋，“卡蒂萨克号”取得了领先。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It seemed certain that she would be the first ship home, but during the race she had a lot of bad luck.
rows.zh: 看来，它一定会最先返回英国，可在比赛中它却接连遭遇不幸。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In August, she was struck by a very heavy storm during which her rudder was torn away.
rows.zh: 八月，它受到一场猛烈风暴的袭击，船舵被风暴扯掉了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Cutty Sark rolled from side to side and it became impossible to steer her.
rows.zh: “卡蒂萨克号”左右摇摆，已经无法操纵方向。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A temporary rudder was made on board from spare planks and it was fitted with great difficulty.
rows.zh: 船员在船上用备用木板做了一只临时船舵，费了很大劲才装上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This greatly reduced the speed of the ship, for there was a danger that if she travelled too quickly, this rudder would be torn away as well.
rows.zh: 这大大降低了航速，因为船一旦开得太快，这只船舵也有被扯掉的危险。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Because of this, the Cutty Sark lost her lead.
rows.zh: 因此，“卡蒂萨克号”失去了领先地位。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After crossing the Equator, the captain called in at a port to have a new rudder fitted, but by now the Thermopylae was over five hundred miles ahead.
rows.zh: 驶过赤道后，船长在一个港口停靠，换装新船舵，可这时“塞莫皮莱号”已领先五百多英里了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though the new rudder was fitted at tremendous speed, it was impossible for the Cutty Sark to win.
rows.zh: 尽管新舵以极快的速度装好了，“卡蒂萨克号”还是不可能获胜了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She arrived in England a week after the Thermopylae.
rows.zh: 它比“塞莫皮莱号”晚一周到达英国。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even this was remarkable, considering that she had had so many delays.
rows.zh: 考虑到它耽搁了这么多次，连这样的成绩也很了不起。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There is no doubt that if she had not lost her rudder she would have won the race easily.
rows.zh: 毫无疑问，如果它没有丢失船舵，本来是能轻松赢得比赛的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: as 后接所起的作用或所承担的角色，不一定指职业。
usage.example: She serves as an impressive reminder of the great ships of the past.
usage.exampleZh: 它让人们鲜明地想起昔日那些巨大的帆船。

usage.note: 强调开始领先的动作；lose one’s lead 表示失去领先优势。

usage.exampleZh: 比赛开始后，两艘船中先到爪哇的是“塞莫皮莱号”，但到了印度洋，“卡蒂萨克号”取得了领先。

usage.note: 表示两侧之间的反复运动，不是从一侧只移动到另一侧一次。

usage.exampleZh: “卡蒂萨克号”左右摇摆，已经无法操纵方向。

usage.note: 也可用于飞机、火车等交通工具；本文指在帆船上制作临时船舵。

usage.exampleZh: 毫无疑问，如果它没有丢失船舵，本来是能轻松赢得比赛的。

rows.en: No one can avoid being influenced by advertisements.
rows.zh: 没有人能够不受广告影响。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Much as we may pride ourselves on our good taste, we are no longer free to choose the things we want, for advertising exerts a subtle influence on us.
rows.zh: 尽管我们可能很为自己的鉴赏力自豪，可我们已无法自由选择想要的东西，因为广告正对我们施加潜移默化的影响。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In their efforts to persuade us to buy this or that product, advertisers have made a close study of human nature and have classified all our little weaknesses.
rows.zh: 广告商为说服我们购买这样那样的产品，深入研究了人性，并把我们所有的小弱点都分门别类。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Advertisers discovered years ago that all of us love to get something for nothing.
rows.zh: 广告商多年前就发现，我们人人都喜欢不花钱就得到东西。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: An advertisement which begins with the magic word FREE can rarely go wrong.
rows.zh: 一则用“免费”这个神奇词语开头的广告，很少会失手。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These days, advertisers not only offer free samples, but free cars, free houses, and free trips round the world as well.
rows.zh: 如今，广告商不仅提供免费样品，还提供免费汽车、免费房屋和免费的环球旅行。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They devise hundreds of competitions which will enable us to win huge sums of money.
rows.zh: 他们设计出几百种竞赛，让我们有机会赢得巨额奖金。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Radio and television have made it possible for advertisers to capture the attention of millions of people in this way.
rows.zh: 广播和电视使广告商能够用这种办法吸引数百万人的注意。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: During a radio programme, a company of biscuit manufacturers once asked listeners to bake biscuits and send them to their factory.
rows.zh: 有一次，一家饼干制造公司在广播节目中请听众烤制饼干，并把成品送到他们的工厂。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They offered to pay $10 a pound for the biggest biscuit baked by a listener.
rows.zh: 他们提出，对听众烤出的最大一块饼干，按每磅十美元付款。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The response to this competition was tremendous.
rows.zh: 这项比赛引起了极大的反响。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Before long, biscuits of all shapes and sizes began arriving at the factory.
rows.zh: 不久，各种形状、各种大小的饼干便开始送到工厂。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One lady brought in a biscuit on a wheelbarrow.
rows.zh: 一位女士用独轮手推车运来了一块饼干。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It weighed nearly 500 pounds.
rows.zh: 它重近五百磅。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A little later, a man came along with a biscuit which occupied the whole boot of his car.
rows.zh: 又过了一会儿，一个男人带来一块饼干，占满了汽车的整个行李厢。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All the biscuits that were sent were carefully weighed.
rows.zh: 所有送来的饼干都经过了仔细称重。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The largest was 713 pounds.
rows.zh: 最大的一块重七百一十三磅。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It seemed certain that this would win the prize.
rows.zh: 看来，这块饼干肯定会获奖。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But just before the competition closed, a lorry arrived at the factory with a truly colossal biscuit which weighed 2,400 pounds.
rows.zh: 可就在比赛快结束时，一辆卡车来到工厂，载着一块真正硕大无比、重达两千四百磅的饼干。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It had been baked by a college student who had used over 1,000 pounds of flour, 800 pounds of sugar, 200 pounds of fat, and 400 pounds of various other ingredients.
rows.zh: 这块饼干是一名大学生烤的，他用了超过一千磅面粉、八百磅糖、两百磅油脂，以及四百磅其他各类配料。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was so heavy that a crane had to be used to remove it from the lorry.
rows.zh: 它重得必须动用起重机，才能从卡车上卸下来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The manufacturers had to pay more money than they had anticipated, for they bought the biscuit from the student for $24,000.
rows.zh: 厂家只好比预想的多花钱，因为他们以两万四千美元的价格向那名学生买下了这块饼干。
rows.speaker: 旁白

lessons.title: Nothing to sell and nothing to buy

rows.en: It has been said that everyone lives by selling something.
rows.zh: 有人说，每个人都靠出售某种东西为生。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the light of this statement, teachers live by selling knowledge, philosophers by selling wisdom and priests by selling spiritual comfort.
rows.zh: 按照这种说法，教师靠出售知识生活，哲学家靠出售智慧生活，牧师则靠出售精神慰藉生活。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though it may be possible to measure the value of material goods in terms of money, it is extremely difficult to estimate the true value of the services which people perform for us.
rows.zh: 物质商品的价值也许可以用金钱衡量，但要估计别人为我们提供的服务究竟价值几何，却极其困难。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There are times when we would willingly give everything we possess to save our lives, yet we might grudge paying a surgeon a high fee for offering us precisely this service.
rows.zh: 有时，我们愿意付出自己拥有的一切来保全性命，可当外科医生恰恰为我们提供这种服务时，我们又可能舍不得付给他高额费用。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The conditions of society are such that skills have to be paid for in the same way that goods are paid for at a shop.
rows.zh: 社会现实如此：技能必须获得报酬，正如在商店购买商品必须付款一样。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Everyone has something to sell.
rows.zh: 每个人都有东西可卖。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Tramps seem to be the only exception to this general rule.
rows.zh: 流浪汉似乎是这条普遍规律的唯一例外。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Beggars almost sell themselves as human beings to arouse the pity of passers-by.
rows.zh: 乞丐为了博取过路人的怜悯，几乎把自己作为人的身份都拿来出卖。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But real tramps are not beggars.
rows.zh: 但真正的流浪汉并不是乞丐。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They have nothing to sell and require nothing from others.
rows.zh: 他们没有东西出售，也不向别人索取什么。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In seeking independence, they do not sacrifice their human dignity.
rows.zh: 他们在追求独立时，并不牺牲自己做人的尊严。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A tramp may ask you for money, but he will never ask you to feel sorry for him.
rows.zh: 流浪汉也许会向你讨钱，但绝不会请求你同情他。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He has deliberately chosen to lead the life he leads and is fully aware of the consequences.
rows.zh: 他是有意选择自己所过的这种生活，而且完全明白其后果。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He may never be sure where the next meal is coming from, but he is free from the thousands of anxieties which afflict other people.
rows.zh: 他也许从来不知道下一顿饭在哪里，可他摆脱了困扰他人的千百种忧虑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: His few material possessions make it possible for him to move from place to place with ease.
rows.zh: 他拥有的物品很少，因此可以轻松地从一处迁往另一处。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: By having to sleep in the open, he gets far closer to the world of nature than most of us ever do.
rows.zh: 由于不得不露宿户外，他与大自然的接近程度，远非我们大多数人所能及。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He may hunt, beg, or steal occasionally to keep himself alive; he may even, in times of real need, do a little work; but he will never sacrifice his freedom.
rows.zh: 他也许偶尔打猎、乞讨或偷窃来维生；真正需要时，甚至可能干一点活；但他绝不肯牺牲自己的自由。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We often speak of tramps with contempt and put them in the same class as beggars, but how many of us can honestly say that we have not felt a little envious of their simple way of life and their freedom from care?
rows.zh: 我们谈起流浪汉，常常满怀鄙夷，把他们与乞丐归为一类；可是，我们中又有几人能坦诚地说，自己从未有一点羡慕他们简朴的生活和无忧无虑呢？
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: by 后接谋生方式，常用动名词；不同于 live on 后接食物或收入来源。

usage.exampleZh: 有人说，每个人都靠出售某种东西为生。

usage.note: 用于依据某种信息、说法或情况重新解释或判断，语气较正式。

usage.exampleZh: 按照这种说法，教师靠出售知识生活，哲学家靠出售智慧生活，牧师则靠出售精神慰藉生活。

usage.note: 引出衡量标准、角度或表达方式，本课以金钱作为价值尺度。
usage.example: Though it may be possible to measure the value of material goods in terms of money, it is extremely difficult to estimate the true value of the services which people perform for us.
usage.exampleZh: 物质商品的价值也许可以用金钱衡量，但要估计别人为我们提供的服务究竟价值几何，却极其困难。

usage.note: of 后接名词性内容；接完整从句时可用 be aware that。

usage.exampleZh: 他是有意选择自己所过的这种生活，而且完全明白其后果。

usage.note: 名词 ease 在此指轻松、不费力；可对应副词 easily。

usage.note: 本文指露宿；其他语境还可指事情公开、不再隐瞒。

usage.exampleZh: 由于不得不露宿户外，他与大自然的接近程度，远非我们大多数人所能及。

rows.en: Small boats loaded with wares sped to the great liner as she was entering the harbour.
rows.zh: 巨型客轮正在驶入港口时，满载货物的小船朝它飞快驶来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Before she had anchored, the men from the boats had climbed on board and the decks were soon covered with colourful rugs from Persia, silks from India, copper coffee pots, and beautiful handmade silverware.
rows.zh: 客轮还未抛锚，小船上的人就已经爬上了船；很快，甲板上摆满了色彩鲜艳的波斯地毯、印度丝绸、铜咖啡壶和精美的手工银器。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was difficult not to be tempted.
rows.zh: 人很难不动心。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Many of the tourists on board had begun bargaining with the tradesmen, but I decided not to buy anything until I had disembarked.
rows.zh: 船上许多游客已经开始与商贩讨价还价，可我决定下船以后再买东西。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I had no sooner got off the ship than I was assailed by a man who wanted to sell me a diamond ring.
rows.zh: 我刚一下船，就被一个想卖钻戒给我的男人缠住了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I had no intention of buying one, but I could not conceal the fact that I was impressed by the size of the diamonds.
rows.zh: 我根本无意买钻戒，却无法掩饰那些钻石的大小给我留下了深刻印象。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Some of them were as big as marbles.
rows.zh: 有些钻石足有玻璃弹珠那么大。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The man went to great lengths to prove that the diamonds were real.
rows.zh: 那人想尽办法，证明钻石是真的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As we were walking past a shop, he held a diamond firmly against the window and made a deep impression in the glass.
rows.zh: 我们路过一家商店时，他把一颗钻石紧压在橱窗玻璃上，在玻璃上划出了一道深痕。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It took me over half an hour to get rid of him.
rows.zh: 我花了半个多小时才摆脱他。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The next man to approach me was selling expensive pens and watches.
rows.zh: 接下来走近我的人，卖的是昂贵的钢笔和手表。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I examined one of the pens closely.
rows.zh: 我仔细查看了其中一支钢笔。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It certainly looked genuine.
rows.zh: 它看起来确实像真货。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At the base of the gold cap, the words ‘made in the U.S.A.’ had been neatly inscribed.
rows.zh: 金色笔帽的底部，整整齐齐地刻着“美国制造”几个字。
rows.speaker: 笔帽铭文

rows.en: The man said that the pen was worth £50, but as a special favour, he would let me have it for £30.
rows.zh: 那人说，这支笔值五十英镑，不过可以特别照顾我，三十英镑就卖给我。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I shook my head and held up five fingers indicating that I was willing to pay £5.
rows.zh: 我摇摇头，伸出五根手指，表示只愿付五英镑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Gesticulating wildly, the man acted as if he found my offer outrageous, but he eventually reduced the price to £10.
rows.zh: 他疯狂地比画着，装出觉得我的出价简直离谱的样子，不过最终还是把价格降到了十英镑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Shrugging my shoulders, I began to walk away when, a moment later, he ran after me and thrust the pen into my hands.
rows.zh: 我耸耸肩，开始往前走；过了一会儿，他追了上来，把笔塞进我手里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though he kept throwing up his arms in despair, he readily accepted the £5 I gave him.
rows.zh: 他虽然不停地绝望地扬起双臂，却爽快地收下了我递过去的五英镑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I felt especially pleased with my wonderful bargain — until I got back to the ship.
rows.zh: 我为这笔绝妙的便宜买卖格外得意——直到回到船上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: No matter how hard I tried, it was impossible to fill this beautiful pen with ink and to this day it has never written a single word!
rows.zh: 无论我怎么努力，都无法给这支漂亮的钢笔灌进墨水；直到今天，它连一个字也没写出来过！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Whether we find a joke funny or not largely depends on where we have been brought up.
rows.zh: 我们是否觉得一个笑话好笑，在很大程度上取决于我们从小在哪里长大。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The sense of humour is mysteriously bound up with national characteristics.
rows.zh: 幽默感与民族特性之间，有着难以解释的密切联系。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A Frenchman, for instance, might find it hard to laugh at a Russian joke.
rows.zh: 例如，法国人可能很难听一个俄国笑话就笑起来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the same way, a Russian might fail to see anything amusing in a joke which would make an Englishman laugh to tears.
rows.zh: 同样，一个俄国人也可能完全看不出某个笑话有何可笑之处，而这个笑话却会使英国人笑出眼泪。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Most funny stories are based on comic situations.
rows.zh: 大多数笑话都建立在滑稽的情境上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In spite of national differences, certain funny situations have a universal appeal.
rows.zh: 尽管存在民族差异，某些滑稽情境却对所有人都有吸引力。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: No matter where you live, you would find it difficult not to laugh at, say, Charlie Chaplin's early films.
rows.zh: 无论你住在哪里，譬如看查理·卓别林的早期电影时，你都会很难忍住不笑。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: However, a new type of humour, which stems largely from the U.S., has recently come into fashion.
rows.zh: 不过，最近一种主要源于美国的新式幽默开始流行。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is called ‘sick humour’.
rows.zh: 它被称为“病态幽默”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Comedians base their jokes on tragic situations like violent death or serious accidents.
rows.zh: 喜剧演员用暴死、严重事故等悲惨情境来编笑话。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Many people find this sort of joke distasteful.
rows.zh: 许多人觉得这类笑话令人反感。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The following example of ‘sick humour’ will enable you to judge for yourself.
rows.zh: 下面这个“病态幽默”的例子，可以让你自行判断。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A man who had broken his right leg was taken to hospital a few weeks before Christmas.
rows.zh: 圣诞节前几个星期，一个摔断右腿的男人被送进了医院。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From the moment he arrived there, he kept on pestering his doctor to tell him when he would be able to go home.
rows.zh: 从进医院那一刻起，他就不断缠着医生，要医生告诉他什么时候能回家。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He dreaded having to spend Christmas in hospital.
rows.zh: 他很害怕不得不在医院过圣诞节。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though the doctor did his best, the patient’s recovery was slow.
rows.zh: 尽管医生竭尽全力，病人的恢复还是很慢。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On Christmas Day, the man still had his right leg in plaster.
rows.zh: 圣诞节那天，他的右腿仍打着石膏。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He spent a miserable day in bed thinking of all the fun he was missing.
rows.zh: 他躺在床上，想着自己错过的种种欢乐，难过地度过了一天。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The following day, however, the doctor consoled him by telling him that his chances of being able to leave hospital in time for New Year celebrations were good.
rows.zh: 然而，第二天，医生安慰他说，他很有希望赶在新年庆祝活动前出院。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The man took heart and, sure enough, on New Year's Eve he was able to hobble along to a party.
rows.zh: 那人振作起来；果然，除夕那天，他已能一瘸一拐地去参加聚会了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: To compensate for his unpleasant experiences in hospital, the man drank a little more than was good for him.
rows.zh: 为了补偿住院时那些不愉快的经历，他喝酒喝得稍微过了量。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the process, he enjoyed himself thoroughly and kept telling everybody how much he hated hospitals.
rows.zh: 在这过程中，他玩得十分尽兴，还不停地告诉大家自己有多么讨厌医院。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He was still mumbling something about hospitals at the end of the party when he slipped on a piece of ice and broke his left leg.
rows.zh: 聚会结束时，他还在含糊地嘟囔着医院的事，忽然踩上一块冰滑了一跤，把左腿摔断了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.exampleZh: 我们是否觉得一个笑话好笑，在很大程度上取决于我们从小在哪里长大。

usage.note: bound up with 强调紧密联系，不是物理意义上捆绑在一起。

usage.exampleZh: 幽默感与民族特性之间，有着难以解释的密切联系。

usage.note: from 引出来源或原因；largely 插在动词与介词之间，表示主要。
usage.example: However, a new type of humour, which stems largely from the U.S., has recently come into fashion.
usage.exampleZh: 不过，最近一种主要源于美国的新式幽默开始流行。

usage.note: come 强调进入流行状态；be in fashion 表示处于流行状态。

usage.exampleZh: 不过，最近一种主要源于美国的新式幽默开始流行。

usage.note: heart 前通常不加冠词；lose heart 则表示灰心。

usage.exampleZh: 那人振作起来；果然，除夕那天，他已能一瘸一拐地去参加聚会了。

usage.note: for 后接损失、缺陷或不快经历，本句指用享乐补偿先前住院的不快。

usage.exampleZh: 为了补偿住院时那些不愉快的经历，他喝酒喝得稍微过了量。

rows.en: For years, villagers believed that Endley Farm was haunted.
rows.zh: 多年来，村民们一直相信恩德利农场闹鬼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The farm was owned by two brothers, Joe and Bob Cox.
rows.zh: 农场属于乔·考克斯和鲍勃·考克斯兄弟俩。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They employed a few farmhands, but no one was willing to work there long.
rows.zh: 他们雇过几个农工，可没有人愿意在那里长干。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Every time a worker gave up his job, he told the same story.
rows.zh: 每当有工人辞职，他都会讲同一个故事。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Farm labourers said that they always woke up to find that work had been done overnight.
rows.zh: 农工们说，他们每次醒来，总会发现活儿已经在夜里干好了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Hay had been cut and cowsheds had been cleaned.
rows.zh: 干草割好了，牛棚也打扫干净了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A farm worker, who stayed up all night, claimed to have seen a figure cutting corn in the moonlight.
rows.zh: 有一个农工一夜没睡，声称看到一个身影在月光下收割庄稼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In time, it became an accepted fact that the Cox brothers employed a conscientious ghost that did most of their work for them.
rows.zh: 久而久之，人们都认定，考克斯兄弟雇了一个尽职尽责的鬼，替他们干了大部分活。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: No one suspected that there might be someone else on the farm who had never been seen.
rows.zh: 没有人想到，农场上也许另有一个从未露过面的人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This was indeed the case.
rows.zh: 实际情况确实如此。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A short time ago, villagers were astonished to learn that the ghost of Endley had died.
rows.zh: 不久前，村民们惊讶地得知，恩德利的那个鬼死了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Everyone went to the funeral, for the ‘ghost’ was none other than Eric Cox, a third brother who was supposed to have died as a young man.
rows.zh: 所有人都去参加了葬礼，因为这个“鬼”不是别人，正是埃里克·考克斯，是兄弟中的另一个，大家一直以为他年轻时就死了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After the funeral, Joe and Bob revealed a secret which they had kept for over fifty years.
rows.zh: 葬礼过后，乔和鲍勃说出了一个他们保守了五十多年的秘密。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Eric had been the eldest son of the family, very much older than his two brothers.
rows.zh: 埃里克是家中的长子，比两个弟弟年长很多。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He had been obliged to join the army during the Second World War.
rows.zh: 第二次世界大战期间，他被迫参了军。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As he hated army life, he decided to desert his regiment.
rows.zh: 由于讨厌军队生活，他决定从所属部队逃走。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When he learnt that he would be sent abroad, he returned to the farm and his father hid him until the end of the war.
rows.zh: 得知自己将被派往国外后，他回到农场，父亲便把他藏了起来，直到战争结束。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Fearing the authorities, Eric remained in hiding after the war as well.
rows.zh: 因为害怕当局追究，战后埃里克也一直躲藏着。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: His father told everybody that Eric had been killed in action.
rows.zh: 父亲告诉所有人，埃里克已经在战斗中阵亡。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The only other people who knew the secret were Joe and Bob.
rows.zh: 除此之外，知道秘密的就只有乔和鲍勃。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They did not even tell their wives.
rows.zh: 他们甚至连妻子都没告诉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When their father died, they thought it their duty to keep Eric in hiding.
rows.zh: 父亲去世后，他们觉得有责任继续把埃里克藏起来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All these years, Eric had lived as a recluse.
rows.zh: 这些年来，埃里克一直过着隐居生活。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He used to sleep during the day and work at night, quite unaware of the fact that he had become the ghost of Endley.
rows.zh: 他白天睡觉、夜里干活，全然不知自己已经成了恩德利的鬼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When he died, however, his brothers found it impossible to keep the secret any longer.
rows.zh: 然而，他死后，两个弟弟再也无法保守这个秘密了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: up 表示仍未上床；stay up all night 指整夜未睡。
usage.example: A farm worker, who stayed up all night, claimed to have seen a figure cutting corn in the moonlight.
usage.exampleZh: 有一个农工一夜没睡，声称看到一个身影在月光下收割庄稼。

usage.note: 本句意为随着时间推移，不是赶在截止时间之前的及时，要结合语境区分。
usage.example: In time, it became an accepted fact that the Cox brothers employed a conscientious ghost that did most of their work for them.
usage.exampleZh: 久而久之，人们都认定，考克斯兄弟雇了一个尽职尽责的鬼，替他们干了大部分活。

usage.note: 用于揭示令人意外的身份，强调就是所说的这个人。
usage.example: Everyone went to the funeral, for the ‘ghost’ was none other than Eric Cox, a third brother who was supposed to have died as a young man.
usage.exampleZh: 所有人都去参加了葬礼，因为这个“鬼”不是别人，正是埃里克·考克斯，是兄弟中的另一个，大家一直以为他年轻时就死了。

usage.note: 表示为避免被发现或抓捕而藏身的状态。

usage.exampleZh: 因为害怕当局追究，战后埃里克也一直躲藏着。

usage.note: 军事用语；本句是父亲向外界提供的说法，随后故事揭示并不属实。

usage.exampleZh: 父亲告诉所有人，埃里克已经在战斗中阵亡。

usage.exampleZh: 他白天睡觉、夜里干活，全然不知自己已经成了恩德利的鬼。
